items.exampleCN: 前缀 over- 标记「越过了限度」。

items.example: Speed gives the measured quantity.
items.exampleCN: speed 提供被测量的那个量。

items.example: Overspeed is the compound itself.
items.exampleCN: overspeed 就是复合词本身。

items.example: The suffix -s forms overspeeds.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -s 构成 overspeeds。

items.example: The suffix -ed forms oversped and overspeeded.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ed 构成 oversped 与 overspeeded。

items.meaningCN: 现在分词与动名词词尾
items.example: The suffix -ing forms overspeeding.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ing 构成 overspeeding。

items.example: Speedy shows the bare adjective at the positive end.
items.exampleCN: speedy 表示「快」的正面一端。

items.meaning: a driver who goes too fast
items.example: Overspeeder adds the person suffix -er.
items.exampleCN: overspeeder 再加上表示人的词尾 -er。

items.meaningCN: 低于；不足（与 over- 相对）
items.example: The prefix under- marks the opposite direction.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 under- 标记相反的方向。

latinEntries.meaningCN: 希望；期待（与 speed 的古法语前身关系存疑，仅作参考）

definition_zh: 夸大；把……说得过分；言过其实
definition_en: to describe something in a way that makes it seem larger, better, or more important than it really is
core_image: 一只被拉到过大的气球，随时要爆开
scene: 记者拿着稿子反复提醒同事，数字和影响都不能写得比事实更重。Do not overstate the benefits of the new policy.
sceneCN: 这里 overstate 是「夸大」，属于第 1 个义项（把事实说得比实际大）；句意：不要夸大新政策的好处。

pos.zh: 夸大；把……说得过分

collocations.zh: 把话说过了头；夸大其词
难以夸大（表示非常重要）

derivatives.zh: 动词加 -ment 构成的名词，指「夸大式说法；言过其实的话」
把前缀换成 under- 的反义词，表示「轻描淡写；少说」
由 understate 加 -ment 构成，表示「轻描淡写；低调的说法」
由过去分词转化的形容词，表示「被夸大的」

senses.title: To describe something as bigger or better than it is
senses.definition: to say that something is larger, better, or more important than it really is
senses.definitionCN: 把某事物的大小、好坏或重要性说得比实际更大
senses.example: The advertisement overstates the benefits of the drink.
senses.exampleCN: 这则广告夸大了这款饮料的好处。
senses.why: Over- means beyond measure and state means to put into words, so to overstate is to set the claim beyond the truth.
senses.whyCN: over- 表示「超过」，state 表示「陈述、说出」，所以 overstate 就是把陈述说得超出事实。

senses.title: To make a claim too strongly
senses.titleCN: 把话说得过头；下定论过猛
senses.definition: to make a statement or judgement with more force than the evidence supports
senses.definitionCN: 作出的陈述或判断比证据所能支撑的力度更强
senses.example: Some critics overstate their case against the reform.
senses.exampleCN: 一些批评者反对这项改革时把话说过了头。
senses.why: From overstating a fact the word moves to overstating an argument, where the force of the claim is what is too much.
senses.whyCN: 从夸大事实进一步延伸到夸大论点，过度的是陈述的力度。

senses.title: Used in the fixed phrase hard to overstate
senses.titleCN: 用于「难以夸大」的固定说法
senses.definition: used in phrases such as hard to overstate to say that something is extremely important
senses.definitionCN: 用于「难以夸大」一类固定说法中，表示某事极为重要
senses.example: It is hard to overstate the value of clean water.
senses.exampleCN: 清洁水源的价值再怎么强调也不为过。
senses.why: Because the verb means to go past the truth, saying it is hard to overstate implies the truth is already enormous.
senses.whyCN: 因为这个词表示「超出事实」，所以说「难以夸大」，等于暗示事实本身已经足够巨大。

senses.title: To exaggerate in a written report
senses.definition: to exaggerate figures or results in a formal account
senses.definitionCN: 在正式报告中夸大数字或结果
senses.example: Several studies overstate the decline in bee numbers.
senses.exampleCN: 多项研究夸大了蜜蜂数量的下降幅度。
senses.why: Reports and statistics give the verb a technical use where the thing overstated is a number.
senses.whyCN: 报告与统计数据使这个词获得一种技术性用法，被夸大的对象具体到数字。

intro.en: Overstate joins the Old English intensive prefix ofer to state, which comes through Old French from Latin status, a standing position.
intro.cn: overstate 由古英语强调前缀 ofer 与 state 组成，而 state 经古法语来自拉丁语 status（站立的姿态）。

items.en: Status means a standing position or condition, from the verb stare, to stand.
items.cn: status 意为站立的姿态或状态，来自动词 stare（站立）。

items.en: Estat keeps the sense of standing as well as rank and condition.
items.cn: 古法语 estat 既保留「站立」的意思，也表示地位、状况。

items.en: State names a condition, a rank, or an important body of people, such as the estates of a realm.
items.cn: 中古英语 state 指状况、地位，或一个重要群体，如一个王国的等级议团。

items.en: State begins to mean to set out in words, giving the verb to state.
items.cn: state 开始表示「用语言陈述」，由此衍生出动词 to state。

items.en: The compound overstate forms by adding the prefix over- in the sense of beyond, and it is common by the nineteenth century.
items.cn: 加上表示「超过」的前缀 over- 之后形成 overstate，到十九世纪已相当常见。

note.en: Overstate pairs state with the over- prefix, and it stands opposite understate while sitting near exaggerate and inflate.
note.cn: overstate 是 state 加 over- 前缀而成的词，与 understate 正好相对，在意义上靠近 exaggerate 与 inflate。

entries.definition: to say or write something in a formal way
entries.definitionCN: 陈述；声明（overstate 的基础词）

entries.definition: a spoken or written declaration
entries.definitionCN: 声明；陈述

entries.definition: to make something seem less than it is
entries.definitionCN: 轻描淡写；少说（overstate 的反义词）

entries.definition: to judge a value as higher than it is
entries.definitionCN: 高估；估计过高（同为 over- 加动词）

entries.definition: to make something seem bigger or better than it is
entries.definitionCN: 夸张；夸大（最常用的同义词）

entries.definition: to make a claim or figure seem larger
entries.definitionCN: 抬高；虚报（数字、价格）

entries.definition: to make something seem more important
entries.definitionCN: 放大；夸大（也与物理上的放大相通）

normalIntro.en: Overstate is over plus state: the stated version has been stretched beyond the true version.
normalIntro.cn: overstate 就是 over 加 state：说出来的版本被拉得比真实版本更大。

normal.en: Over- carries the sense of beyond, so overstate is to state beyond the truth.
normal.cn: over- 表示「超出」，所以 overstate 就是「说过了事实」。

normal.en: Understate is its direct opposite, formed by swapping the prefix.
normal.cn: understate 是它的直接反义词，只把前缀一换。

normal.en: Overstate the case is the fixed phrase for arguing more strongly than the facts allow.
normal.cn: overstate the case 是固定搭配，指论点比事实所能支撑的更猛。

normal.en: Cannot be overstated means the truth is already very big.
normal.cn: cannot be overstated 表示事实已经足够大，无需再加。

normal.en: Its noun is overstatement, built with the -ment suffix.
normal.cn: 它的名词形式 overstatement 由后缀 -ment 构成。

abstract.en: Picture a balloon blown far past the size it was made for.
abstract.cn: 想象一只气球被吹得远远超过原本的尺寸。

abstract.en: Imagine a small puddle painted as if it were a lake.
abstract.cn: 想象一滩小水洼被画成了一片湖。

abstract.en: Think of a speech where every number is pushed one zero to the right.
abstract.cn: 想象一场演讲里，每个数字都被多加了一个零。

examples.en: Politicians often overstate the risks in plans of their opponents.
examples.cn: 政客常常夸大对手计划的风险。

examples.en: The difficulty of the final exam cannot be overstated.
examples.cn: 期末考试之难，再怎么强调也不为过。

examples.en: If anything, the report understates the pressure on small farms.
examples.cn: 报告对小型农场承受的压力其实说得还算轻。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「欧沃-斯特」——说起话来先「呜呜」地加码，把话说得比事实更「特」别；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: over（超过，源自古英语 ofer）+ state（陈述，源自拉丁 status 站立、状态，经古法语 estat 入英语）→ 把陈述说得超过事实，即「夸大」。

sensesIntro.en: Overstate starts with stretching a fact, then stretches an argument, then appears inside the fixed phrase hard to overstate, and finally names inflated figures in reports.
sensesIntro.cn: overstate 先是把事实拉大，再把论点拉大，随后进入「难以夸大」这类固定说法，最后用来指报告中虚增的数字。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a statement stretched beyond what is true.
core.cn: 核心意象：一句话被拉得超过事实。

branches.en: The everyday sense enlarges facts in ordinary speech.
branches.cn: 日常用法就是在平常说话中把事实放大。

branches.en: In an argument the thing stretched is the force of the claim.
branches.cn: 在辩论里被拉大的是论点的力度。

branches.en: The fixed phrase uses the stretched idea in reverse.
branches.cn: 固定说法把「拉大」的意思反过来用。

branches.en: Both speech and reports can inflate what is said.
branches.cn: 口头话语与书面报告都会虚增所述内容。

branches.en: In both cases the speaker goes past the evidence.
branches.cn: 两种情形里，说话人都越过了证据的边界。

intro.en: Overstate puts the prefix over in front of the verb state, and its family also includes understate and overstatement.
intro.cn: overstate 把前缀 over 放在动词 state 之前，同族词还有 understate 与 overstatement。

latinIntro.en: State descends from Latin status and stare, while the prefix over is Germanic and the pair joined in English.
latinIntro.cn: state 源自拉丁语 status 与 stare，而前缀 over 属日耳曼语系，两者在英语里才组合起来。

items.example: The prefix over- marks excess.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 over- 标记「过量」。

items.example: State supplies the speaking element.
items.exampleCN: state 提供「说」的那一部分。

items.meaning: to say more than is true
items.example: Overstate is the compound verb.
items.exampleCN: overstate 就是复合动词本身。

items.meaningCN: 表示「行为或结果」的名词词尾
items.example: The suffix -ment forms overstatement.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ment 构成 overstatement。

items.example: The prefix under- forms understate.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 under- 构成 understate。

items.example: The suffix -s forms overstates.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -s 构成 overstates。

items.example: The suffix -ed forms overstated.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ed 构成 overstated。

items.example: The suffix -ing forms overstating.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ing 构成 overstating。

items.example: Statement keeps the meaning of what is said.
items.exampleCN: statement 保留「被说出的话」这一含义。

definition_zh: 概观；概述；总体看法
definition_en: a general description or broad view of something, covering its main points but not its details
core_image: 人站上高台远望，整片田野的轮廓一眼尽收
scene: 新员工上岗先听主管介绍项目全貌。The manager gave the new staff a quick overview of the project.
sceneCN: 这里 overview 是「概述、总体介绍」（第 1 个义项：概括说明某事的总体情况）；句意：经理给新员工简单概述了这个项目。

pos.zh: 概观；概述；总体印象
总览的；总体性的（如总览图）

derivatives.zh: 由 over 加 view 构成的复合词，去前缀后回到基础词，义为「看法；观看」
view 加表人的后缀 -er，指观看者，可见同族词共享「看」的核心
view 加 point（点），指看问题的视角；与 overview 同属「看」的家族
re- 表示再、回，加 view 表示回过头再看，因而引申为「评论；复习」
pre- 表示在前，加 view 表示提前看，因而指「预览；预映」

senses.title: A general summary
senses.definition: a short general description of the main points of a subject or document
senses.definitionCN: 对某主题或文件要点所作的简短、总体性说明
senses.example: The report opens with a one-page overview of the findings.
senses.exampleCN: 报告开头用一页篇幅概述了研究发现。
senses.why: Over adds the idea of looking from above, so an overview is a description that skips details and shows only the shape of the whole.
senses.whyCN: over 带来「从上往下看」的意思，所以概述是略去细节、只呈现整体轮廓的那种说明。

senses.title: A bird view understanding
senses.definition: a mental picture in which a person understands the whole situation rather than isolated facts
senses.definitionCN: 心中对整体局势的了解，而非零散事实
senses.example: Reading the map gave us a better overview of the region.
senses.exampleCN: 看了地图，我们对这一地区有了更好的总体了解。
senses.why: Once the view is lifted high enough, the mind picture itself counts as the overview, not only the sentences that describe it.
senses.whyCN: 一旦视线升得足够高，头脑中的那幅全景图本身就算作 overview，而不只是描述它的语句。

senses.title: A survey of a field
senses.definition: a text or talk that surveys the state of a field of study for readers who are new to it
senses.definitionCN: 为初学者梳理某一学科现状的文章或讲座
senses.example: The lecture is an overview of modern banking law.
senses.exampleCN: 这场讲座是对现代银行法的概览。
senses.why: A survey stands like a viewing platform from which students can see the whole landscape of a discipline before walking into its details.
senses.whyCN: 综述好比一座观景台，学生由此先看到整个学科的版图，然后再走进细节。

senses.title: A scene as it appears from above
senses.definition: a view of a place seen from a high position, as from a hill or an aircraft
senses.definitionCN: 从高处如山顶或飞机上看到的某地景象
senses.example: From the ridge, the hikers had an overview of the valley.
senses.exampleCN: 站在山脊上，徒步者俯瞰着整个山谷。
senses.why: This is the literal scene behind the word: a high place from which the eye covers a wide area at once, and the abstract senses borrow its power.
senses.whyCN: 这是词义的字面场景：站在高处，视线一次覆盖广阔区域；抽象义项都借用了这种力量。

senses.title: A summary slide or section
senses.definition: a section or slide in a document or presentation that summarises the parts that follow
senses.definitionCN: 文件或演示中用来概括后续内容的章节或幻灯片
senses.example: The slide deck ends with an overview of the costs.
senses.exampleCN: 演示文稿最后一页概述了各项成本。
senses.why: A modern document needs a page that stands above the rest, so the planning word came to name that opening or closing panel.
senses.whyCN: 现代文件需要一页统摄其余内容的部分，于是规划词的名号被用来指这样的首页或尾页。

intro.en: Overview joins the prefix over, from Old English ofer, with view, from Old French veue, a seeing, which goes back to Latin videre, to see.
intro.cn: overview 由前缀 over（源自古英语 ofer）与 view（源自古法语 veue「看见」，上溯拉丁语 videre「看」）组合而成。

items.en: Videre means to see, and the past participle visus supplies the family of words about sight.
items.cn: videre 意为「看」，其过去分词 visus 提供了表示视觉的词族。

items.en: Ofer means over or above, the same form that still heads words like overlook and overdraft.
items.cn: ofer 意为「在上方」，今天 overlook、overdraft 等词仍以同样的形式开头。

items.en: Veue means a sight or a seeing, and English borrows it as view.
items.cn: veue 意为「景象、看见」，英语借入为 view。

items.en: Over and view are first joined in the sense of seeing over an area, as from a height.
items.cn: over 与 view 起初结合，表示从高处望过一片区域。

items.en: The word settles into offices and classrooms as the name for a general summary or survey.
items.cn: 这个词后来进入办公室与课堂，用来指总体概述或综述。

note.en: Overview is a compound built on view, so it keeps company with the view family and with plain summary words.
note.cn: overview 是以 view 为词干的复合词，因此与 view 词族以及普通的「概括」类词相邻。

entries.definition: to look at something, or what can be seen from a place
entries.definitionCN: 看；视野；看法

entries.definition: to look again at something in order to judge or study it
entries.definitionCN: 复查；评论；复习

entries.definition: a chance to see something before it is shown to everyone
entries.definitionCN: 预览；预映

entries.definition: a short account of the main points of something
entries.definitionCN: 摘要；总结

entries.definition: a general plan or a line that shows only the main shape
entries.definitionCN: 大纲；轮廓

entries.definition: a general examination of a subject or an area
entries.definitionCN: 综述；勘测

normalIntro.en: Overview is over plus view: a view taken from above, so the details blur and the shape of the whole stays clear.
normalIntro.cn: overview 就是 over 加 view：从上方取景，细节变模糊，整体轮廓却清楚。

normal.en: Give an overview of means to say how the whole thing works, in a few sentences.
normal.cn: 「give an overview of」就是用几句话说明整件事如何运转。

normal.en: An overview is never complete; it deliberately leaves out the small parts.
normal.cn: 概述从不求完整，它故意略去细枝末节。

normal.en: Compare overview with review: one looks from above, the other looks again.
normal.cn: 对比 overview 与 review：前者从上方看，后者再看一遍。

normal.en: In a report the overview section comes first, so readers know where they are going.
normal.cn: 报告中的概述部分放在最前，让读者先知道要走到哪里。

normal.en: A broad overview is wider than a brief overview, because broad describes scope and brief describes length.
normal.cn: a broad overview 比 a brief overview 更宽，因为 broad 说范围，brief 说篇幅。

abstract.en: Imagine a map on the wall with every street drawn but no house numbers.
abstract.cn: 想象墙上挂着一张画满街道却没有门牌号的地图。

abstract.en: Think of a pilot looking down at a city that becomes a pattern of blocks.
abstract.cn: 想象飞行员俯视一座城市，整座城化成一片街区拼图。

abstract.en: Picture a lecture hall where the first slide shows a single diagram of the whole course.
abstract.cn: 想象课堂上的第一张幻灯片只有一幅贯穿全课程的图。

examples.en: She gave a brief overview of the company finances.
examples.cn: 她简要概述了公司的财务状况。

examples.en: An overview map on the first page shows each chapter at a glance.
examples.cn: 首页的总览图把每一章都一眼呈现出来。

examples.en: The textbook has a short historical overview before the main chapters.
examples.cn: 这本教材在正文之前有一段简短的历史概况。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「欧味秀」——站在欧洲的高台上俯瞰一场大秀，全场尽收眼底；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 古英语 ofer（在……上方）+ 古法语 veue（看见）→ 英语 overview，字面义「从上方看见」，核心义「一览全局的概述」。

sensesIntro.en: Overview runs from a high view of a place, through a general summary and the mental picture it leaves, to a survey of a field and a summary section of a document.
sensesIntro.cn: overview 从对某地的俯瞰出发，经过总体概述与由此留下的整体印象，延伸到学科综述与文件里的概要部分。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: standing on a height and taking in the whole land at one glance.
core.cn: 核心意象：站在高处，一眼望尽整片大地。

branches.en: A short general description is the everyday sense of the noun.
branches.cn: 简短的总体说明是这个词最日常的义项。

branches.en: The high view becomes the mind picture a reader carries away.
branches.cn: 高处所见转化为读者带走的那幅整体印象。

branches.en: A survey of a field is the overview written for newcomers.
branches.cn: 学科综述是为初学者写的概览。

branches.en: The literal view from a hill or aircraft keeps the spatial core intact.
branches.cn: 从山顶或飞机上看到的景象保留了完整的空间内核。

branches.en: A summary slide or section is the summary sense frozen into a document.
branches.cn: 概要页或总览章节是概述义在文件中的固定形态。

intro.en: Overview is a modern compound of over and view, so its build is best read through two old words rather than through a Latin stem.
intro.cn: overview 是 over 与 view 的现代复合词，理解它主要靠这两个古老单词，而不是某个拉丁词干。

latinIntro.en: The view part goes back to Latin videre, to see, whose participle supplies many words of sight.
latinIntro.cn: 其中的 view 可上溯拉丁语 videre「看」，其分词形式衍生出许多表示视觉的词。

items.example: The prefix over- makes over look above.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 over- 让 over 带有在上的意味。

items.example: Ofer is the early form behind the prefix.
items.exampleCN: ofer 是这个前缀背后的早期形式。

items.example: A view is what the eye takes in.
items.exampleCN: view 是眼睛收进的一切。

items.example: The suffix -er marks the person who views.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -er 标出观看的人。

items.meaning: a point from which one looks
items.example: View and point combine into a standpoint.
items.exampleCN: view 与 point 合成为立足点。

items.meaning: re- plus view, a looking again
items.example: The prefix re- in review adds the idea of looking again.
items.exampleCN: review 中的前缀 re- 加上回看之意。

items.meaning: pre- plus view, a looking before
items.example: The prefix pre- in preview means before.
items.exampleCN: preview 中的前缀 pre- 表示在前。

items.meaning: a person who is looked at closely
items.example: The taker of an interaction is called an interviewee.
items.exampleCN: 被采访交流的一方称为 interviewee。

items.meaning: to look the whole of something over
items.example: A survey covers a field the way an overview does.
items.exampleCN: survey 像 overview 一样总览一片领域。

items.meaning: the outer line or main shape
items.example: An outline keeps only the line around things.
items.exampleCN: outline 只保留事物外围的线。

definition_zh: 超重的；肥胖的；超重；超额负担
definition_en: heavier than is healthy or allowed, or an amount of weight, luggage, or burden that goes beyond a limit
core_image: 秤盘上的指针越过刻度线，重量压过了允许的那一格
scene: 医生量完学生的身高体重，提醒他体重已超标。The doctor told him that he was slightly overweight.
sceneCN: 这里 overweight 是「超重的、偏胖的」（第 1 个义项：体重超过健康标准）；句意：医生告诉他体重略超标。

pos.zh: 超重的；肥胖的
超重；超出限额的重量
使负担过重；使超载（较少用）

derivatives.zh: 去掉 over 后的基础词，义为「重量；称重」，可见复合词的核心在 weight
over 加 weigh，指重得超过对方或令人不堪重负，与 overweight 共享超量之意
under 表示不足，加 weight 即「体重不足」，是 overweight 的直接反义
weight 加形容词后缀 -y，义为「沉重的；有分量的」，同族里最具体的一支
weight 加 -less，义为「无重量的；失重的」，与「超重」形成两极对照

senses.title: Heavier than healthy
senses.definition: weighing more than is healthy for a person of a given height and build
senses.definitionCN: 对于某一身高体格的人而言，体重超过健康水平
senses.example: The school now screens every pupil for being overweight.
senses.exampleCN: 学校现在为每个学生筛查是否超重。
senses.why: Over marks a line passed and weight is the measured pounds, so the adjective first describes a body that has gone past the medical limit.
senses.whyCN: over 标记越过的界线，weight 是称出的磅数，所以这个形容词首先描述越过医学标准线的身体。

senses.title: Beyond a weight allowance
senses.definition: weighing more than a rule allows, as with luggage, vehicles, or loads
senses.definitionCN: 重量超过规定限额，如行李、车辆或货物
senses.example: The airline charges extra for overweight bags.
senses.exampleCN: 航空公司对超重行李额外收费。
senses.why: Transport and trade need fixed limits, and any object passing them wears the same label as a passing body.
senses.whyCN: 运输与贸易需要固定限额，任何越过限额的物品都被贴上与身体相同的标签。

senses.title: An excess weight as a noun
senses.definition: the amount by which something weighs more than it should, or the state of carrying such an excess
senses.definitionCN: 某物超出应有标准的重量，或处于荷载过量的状态
senses.example: The ship listed slightly because of an overweight in the hold.
senses.exampleCN: 因货舱超载，船体略微倾斜。
senses.why: Once weight becomes a thing that can be counted, the excess itself is named by the same compound.
senses.whyCN: 一旦重量成为可以计数的事物，多出来的那部分就用同一个复合词来命名。

senses.title: Burdened with an excess
senses.definition: carrying too much of something, often duties or debt, so that the whole is strained
senses.definitionCN: 承载过多之物——常是职责或债务——以致整体不堪重负
senses.example: A portfolio that is overweight in one sector can lose value fast.
senses.exampleCN: 过度押注单一行业的投资组合可能迅速贬值。
senses.why: The scale image moves to finance: too much of one thing on the tray tips the balance, just as too many kilos tilt the pointer.
senses.whyCN: 秤的意象转到金融：托盘上某样东西太多就会打破平衡，正如过多的公斤数压歪指针。

senses.title: More weight than the other side
senses.definition: weighing more than another person or thing, so as to tip a scale or a contest
senses.definitionCN: 比另一方更重，从而在秤上或较量中压过对方
senses.example: In the final bout the heavier fighter clearly overweights his rival.
senses.exampleCN: 在最后一场对决中，较重的拳手明显压过对手。
senses.why: The older verb overweigh treats over as more than, and this sense keeps that plain comparison alive.
senses.whyCN: 较早的动词 overweigh 把 over 理解为「多于」，这个义项保留了这种直白的比较。

intro.en: Overweight is a compound of over, which appears in English by the 10th century, and weight, from Old English gewiht.
intro.cn: overweight 由 over 与 weight 复合而成：over 在十世纪已见于英语，weight 来自古英语 gewiht。

items.en: A reconstructed west Germanic form behind gewiht suggests the sense of carrying or weighing.
items.cn: gewiht 背后可重构的西日耳曼语形式暗示「承载、称量」之意。

items.en: Gewiht means a weight or a load, and it slowly loses its prefix in Middle English.
items.cn: gewiht 意为重量或负荷，中古英语时期前缀逐渐脱落。

items.en: Wieght and later weight settle the spelling of the noun.
items.cn: wieght 以及后来的 weight 确定了名词的拼写。

items.en: Over and weight join to describe a load or a body above the allowed measure.
items.cn: over 与 weight 结合，用来描述超过允许刻度的负荷或身体。

items.en: Medical use makes overweight a standard health label for excess body weight.
items.cn: 医学用法让 overweight 成为描述体重超标的标准健康标签。

note.en: Overweight belongs to the weight family and to the whole set of over-prefixed words, and it sits beside obesity and chubby in meaning.
note.cn: overweight 属于 weight 词族与整组以 over 开头的词，在意思上又与 obesity、chubby 相邻。

entries.definition: how heavy something is, or a heavy load
entries.definitionCN: 重量；重物

entries.definition: to weigh more than something else or to burden it
entries.definitionCN: 重于；使负担过重

entries.definition: weighing less than is healthy
entries.definitionCN: 体重不足的

entries.definition: extremely overweight in a medical sense
entries.definitionCN: 肥胖的（医学用语）

entries.definition: slightly fat in a pleasing way
entries.definitionCN: 胖乎乎的（口语，偏可爱）

entries.definition: large and heavy in body
entries.definitionCN: 肥胖的（书面语）

normalIntro.en: Overweight is over plus weight: the weight has gone over the line, whether on a bathroom scale or on an airline counter.
normalIntro.cn: overweight 就是 over 加 weight：重量越过了线，无论是在浴室的体重秤上还是在机场柜台。

normal.en: Keep the pairs straight: overweight is the state, overweigh is the verb.
normal.cn: 分清两对：overweight 是状态，overweigh 是动词。

normal.en: Underweight and overweight are one prefix apart, and both follow weight.
normal.cn: underweight 与 overweight 只差一个前缀，都以 weight 结尾。

normal.en: The same prefix marks many over- words: overdue, overate, overfill.
normal.cn: 同一前缀标记许多 over 开头的词：overdue、overate、overfill。

normal.en: Luggage is overweight when it passes the airline limit.
normal.cn: 行李超重，就是超过了航空公司的限额。

normal.en: Becoming overweight is a process; being overweight is a state.
normal.cn: become overweight 是过程；be overweight 是状态。

abstract.en: Picture a needle sliding past a red mark on a dial.
abstract.cn: 想象指针滑过表盘上的红色刻度。

abstract.en: Think of a suitcase that will not close until someone sits on it.
abstract.cn: 想象一只行李箱，非得有人坐上去才关得合。

abstract.en: Imagine a loan piled so high that the desk bends under it.
abstract.cn: 想象一摞贷款堆得太高，压得桌子都弯了。

examples.en: Doctors warn that more children are overweight than ever before.
examples.cn: 医生警告说，如今超重的孩子比以往任何时候都多。

examples.en: She had to pay an overweight fee for her suitcase.
examples.cn: 她不得不为行李箱支付超重费。

examples.en: The airline lists overweight charges clearly online.
examples.cn: 这家航空公司在网上清楚列出了超重费标准。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「欧沃威特」——体重压得人直喊「威特」；只是谐音，与词源无关，真正的记忆点是 over（超过）加 weight（重量）。

root: 古英语 ofer（超过、在上方）+ 古英语 gewiht（重量）→ 中古英语 weight → 复合为 overweight，核心义「重量超过限度」。

sensesIntro.en: Overweight starts with an over-heavy body, then an overweight bag, then the excess weight itself, then an overloaded portfolio, and lastly the plain act of outweighing.
sensesIntro.cn: overweight 先指过重的身体，再指超重的行李，接着指出超出的重量本身、超载的投资组合，最后回到「重于对方」的直白比较。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the needle on a scale moving past the red line.
core.cn: 核心意象：秤上的指针越过红线。

branches.en: An over-heavy body is the medical sense that dominates today.
branches.cn: 过重的身体是今天占主导的医学义项。

branches.en: An over-heavy bag carries the same line into trade and travel.
branches.cn: 超重的行李把同一条界线带进贸易与旅行。

branches.en: The excess weight itself is the noun sense of the compound.
branches.cn: 超出的重量本身就是这个复合词的名词义项。

branches.en: An overloaded portfolio turns the scale into a metaphor for burden.
branches.cn: 超载的投资组合把秤变成负担的隐喻。

branches.en: Weighing more than a rival returns to the plain comparative reading of over.
branches.cn: 重于对手则回到 over 最直白的比较含义。

intro.en: Overweight is built from a Germanic prefix and a Germanic noun, so the latin part below only explains the deeper family of weight.
intro.cn: overweight 由日耳曼语系的前缀与名词构成，下面所列的拉丁同族只说明 weight 更深一层的亲缘。

latinIntro.en: The Latin verb vehere carries the sense of bearing or moving a load, and its noun vexare grows from the same idea of shaking and straining.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语动词 vehere 带有承载、运送负荷的意思，其衍生的动词 vexare 也由「摇晃、拉扯」的同一观念生长出来。

items.example: The prefix over- marks a measure that is passed.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 over- 标出越过的尺度。

items.example: The older root behind wear carries loads on the body.
items.exampleCN: wear 背后的古老词根指在身上承载。

items.example: Weight is the noun at the centre of the compound.
items.exampleCN: weight 是这个复合词的核心名词。

items.example: The suffix -y forms weighty, meaning heavy.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -y 构成 weighty，意为沉重。

items.example: The suffix -less forms weightless, meaning without weight.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -less 构成 weightless，意为失重的。

items.example: The prefix under- makes underweight the opposite word.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 under- 让 underweight 成为反义词。

items.example: The prefix out- exceeds a rival as out- in outperform does.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 out- 表示胜过对手，如 outperform。

items.example: Overdue shares the same prefix of passing a limit.
items.exampleCN: overdue 共享同一「越过限度」的前缀。

items.example: Overeat applies the prefix to food as overweight applies it to the body.
items.exampleCN: overeat 把前缀用于食物，正如 overweight 用于身体。

definition_zh: 压倒；使受不了；淹没；压倒性击败
definition_en: to be so strong or so much that someone or something is completely covered, defeated, or unable to cope
core_image: 大浪高出堤岸，把岸边的一切整个翻盖过去
scene: 灾后求助电话一个接一个，接线员忙不过来。The small charity was overwhelmed by offers of help.
sceneCN: 这里 overwhelm 是「压得人应付不过来」（第 1 个义项：情势过强使人无法招架）；句意：这家小慈善机构被蜂拥而至的援助提议压得应付不过来。

pos.zh: 压倒；使受不了；使不知所措
淹没；覆盖
压倒性击败
被压垮的；受宠若惊的（用于过去分词）

derivatives.zh: overwhelm 加 -ing，由动作转成性质，义为「压倒性的；难以抵挡的」
overwhelming 加 -ly 构成副词，义为「压倒性地」
由 wheel（轮）与古词 helm（盖）复合，指像浪头整体盖下来的，与 overwhelm 同根
un- 加 whelm（覆盖），与 overwhelm 相对，义为「不被压倒；泰然处之」（少用）
去掉 over 的基础动词，义为「盖没；涌没」（古旧用法）

senses.title: To overpower by sheer amount
senses.definition: to defeat or disable someone by being too great in amount, force, or demand
senses.definitionCN: 因数量、力量或要求过大而使某人无法招架
senses.example: Requests flooded in so fast that staff were overwhelmed.
senses.exampleCN: 请求来得太快，员工们应接不暇。
senses.why: The over- prefix marks something above, and whelm meant to turn over or cover, so the first sense is a weight too great to stand upright under.
senses.whyCN: 前缀 over- 表示在上方，whelm 原意为翻转、覆盖，所以第一义项就是重到无法站直承受的分量。

senses.title: To flood completely
senses.definition: to cover something entirely with a large flow of water or similar mass
senses.definitionCN: 用大股水流或类似的量完全覆盖某物
senses.example: The river burst its banks and overwhelmed the lower streets.
senses.exampleCN: 河水冲垮河岸，淹没了地势较低的街道。
senses.why: Whelming once pictured a wave rolling over a boat, so the water sense keeps the most concrete image of all.
senses.whyCN: whelm 一度描绘巨浪翻过船身，所以「水」的义项保留了最具体的画面。

senses.title: To leave someone emotionally shaken
senses.definition: to make someone feel too much shock, grief, or gratitude to act normally
senses.definitionCN: 使某人因震惊、悲伤或感激过量而无法如常应对
senses.example: She was overwhelmed with gratitude when the whole class helped.
senses.exampleCN: 全班同学都来帮忙时，她感激得不知所措。
senses.why: Feelings arrive like a tide, and when they pour over the mind in one wave the person is said to be overwhelmed rather than merely glad or sad.
senses.whyCN: 情绪像潮水涌来，一旦一波盖过整个心绪，人就叫 overwhelmed，而不只是高兴或难过。

senses.title: To rout in battle
senses.definition: to beat an opponent completely and decisively, so that organised resistance collapses
senses.definitionCN: 彻底而决定性地击败对手，使有组织的抵抗瓦解
senses.example: The home side overwhelmed the visitors in the second half.
senses.exampleCN: 主队在下半场彻底压垮了客队。
senses.why: In battle the side that sweeps over the other like a wave wins outright, so the flood image became a word for total victory.
senses.whyCN: 战场上如潮水般漫过对手的一方会获胜，于是「大水」的意象转为「彻底击败」。

senses.title: To weigh down with excess
senses.definition: to load or burden someone with so much of something that it becomes a hardship
senses.definitionCN: 以过多的某物加载某人，使之成为重负
senses.example: Do not overwhelm the new interns with paperwork.
senses.exampleCN: 不要用成堆的文书把新实习生压得喘不过气。
senses.why: A loaded boat that sits below the waterline is weighed down by cargo, and the verb extends that picture to duties and demands.
senses.whyCN: 载货的船沉到吃水线以下，就是被货物压住，这个动词把这幅画面延伸到处务与要求。

senses.title: An overpowering share of votes
senses.definition: to win or gain by so wide a margin that the result cannot be doubted
senses.definitionCN: 以极大差距获胜或占有，使结果无可置疑
senses.example: Supporters overwhelmed opponents at the polling station by three to one.
senses.exampleCN: 支持者以三比一在投票站压倒了对手。
senses.why: Because the prefix names an excess, any margin that looks like a wave over a shore is called overwhelming.
senses.whyCN: 由于前缀本身表示过量，任何如浪头漫岸般的悬殊差距都被称作压倒性的。

intro.en: Overwhelm joins over with the old verb whelm, and the uncertain part is how whelm itself began.
intro.cn: overwhelm 由 over 与古动词 whelm 结合而成，其中最不确定的部分是 whelm 自身的来历。

items.en: Whelm is recorded with the sense of turning over or covering, and its deeper origin is uncertain.
items.cn: whelm 见于古英语，意为翻转或覆盖，但更深的来源不确定。

items.en: Whelmen keeps the covering sense, and the compound overwhelmen appears as a stronger form of it.
items.cn: whelmen 保留「覆盖」之意，复合词 overwhelmen 作为更强的形式出现。

items.en: The compound name a flood or a force that sweeps over a person or a place.
items.cn: 这个复合词指漫过人或地方的洪水或力量。

items.en: Doctrine and poetry use the verb for troops and grief alike, widening the range.
items.cn: 在政论与诗文中，它既指军队也指悲伤，用法范围随之扩大。

items.en: Business, medicine, and computing all borrow the word for demand and data that grow too fast.
items.cn: 今天的商务、医学与计算机领域都借用它，指增长过快的要求与数据。

note.en: Overwhelm pairs with its own family of whelm words and with a set of verbs about flooding and defeating.
note.cn: overwhelm 一面属于 whelm 词族，一面向「淹没」与「击败」两类动词延伸。

entries.definition: to cover or submerge, now mostly archaic
entries.definitionCN: 盖没；淹没（今多属古旧用法）

entries.definition: rolling over something like a wave
entries.definitionCN: 像浪头整体盖下的

entries.definition: so strong that it cannot be resisted
entries.definitionCN: 压倒性的；难以抵挡的

entries.definition: to go completely under water
entries.definitionCN: 淹没；浸没

entries.definition: to cover or flood something with a great quantity
entries.definitionCN: 淹没；使应接不暇

entries.definition: to defeat completely or press out of shape
entries.definitionCN: 压碎；彻底击败

normalIntro.en: Overwhelm is over plus whelm, an old word for covering: something pours over you until nothing of you is left uncovered.
normalIntro.cn: overwhelm 就是 over 加 whelm，后者是古体的「覆盖」：有东西一直漫过你，直到你身上没有一处还剩在外面。

normal.en: Be overwhelmed by is the standard frame, so learn the passive early.
normal.cn: be overwhelmed by 是标准句式，尽早掌握被动用法。

normal.en: The adjective overwhelming describes the force; the verb overwhelm describes the act.
normal.cn: 形容词 overwhelming 描述力量，动词 overwhelm 描述动作。

normal.en: Overwhelm with takes what is poured: delight, questions, forms, notices.
normal.cn: overwhelm with 后面接被倾泻之物：喜悦、问题、表格、通知。

normal.en: Compare overwhelm and under pressure: one is a flood, the other a steady push.
normal.cn: 对比压力：overwhelm 是洪水漫顶，普通压力则是持续的推。

normal.en: Overwhelmingly is the adverb of margins, as in voting overwhelmingly.
normal.cn: overwhelmingly 是表示悬殊差距的副词，如 voting overwhelmingly。

abstract.en: Picture a wave rising well above a sea wall and spilling across the road.
abstract.cn: 想象一道浪升得远高于海堤，漫过整条公路。

abstract.en: Imagine an inbox filling faster than a hand can empty it.
abstract.cn: 想象收件箱堆积的速度快于一只手清空它的速度。

abstract.en: Think of a crowd cheering so loudly that a single voice cannot be heard at all.
abstract.cn: 想象人群的欢呼太响，以致一个声音完全听不见。

examples.en: The charity was overwhelmed with donations after the flood.
examples.cn: 洪灾之后，这家慈善机构被铺天盖地的捐赠弄得应接不暇。

examples.en: Fans swarmed into the tiny stadium hours before kickoff.
examples.cn: 球赛开始前几小时，球迷就涌进了这座小体育场。

examples.en: He felt overwhelmed by the size of the task ahead.
examples.cn: 面对任务的规模，他感到不堪重负。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「欧沃威欧姆」——过大的电流把欧姆表都压爆了；这只是谐音，与词源无关，真实的记忆点是 over（压在上方）加 whelm（盖没）。

root: 古英语 ofer（在上方、越过）+ whelm（翻转、盖没，深层来源不确定）→ 英语 overwhelm，核心义「如大浪盖顶而来」。

sensesIntro.en: Overwhelm begins with force too great to stand under, keeps its literal flood, then moves to feelings, to defeat in battle, to burdens, and finally to any overwhelming margin.
sensesIntro.cn: overwhelm 从「重得站不住」开始，保留「大水漫盖」的字面义，再走向情绪、战场、负担，最后落到任何「压倒性」的悬殊差距。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a great wave rising over the bank and covering everything behind it.
core.cn: 核心意象：大浪高出堤岸，把岸后的一切都盖住。

branches.en: Too much arriving at once is the dominant modern sense.
branches.cn: 过量的东西同时涌来，是今天最主要的义项。

branches.en: A real flood covering the streets is the literal sense.
branches.cn: 真实洪水漫过街道，是字面义项。

branches.en: Feelings pouring over the mind are the emotional branch.
branches.cn: 情绪漫过心绪，是情感分支。

branches.en: Sweeping over an army gives the sense of decisive defeat.
branches.cn: 如潮水漫过军队，得出「彻底击败」的义项。

branches.en: A boat sunk by cargo becomes a picture for burdens and for wide vote margins.
branches.cn: 被货物压沉的船成为负担与悬殊票差的画面。

intro.en: Overwhelm is a prefix plus an old English verb, and the prefix does most of the visible work.
intro.cn: overwhelm 由一个前缀加一个古英语动词构成，显眼的工作主要由前缀承担。

latinIntro.en: The Latin below follows the flood image inside the word, though overwhelm itself comes straight from Old English.
latinIntro.cn: 下面的拉丁同族顺着词内的「大水」意象延伸，不过 overwhelm 本身直接源自古英语。

items.example: The prefix over- puts the force above the head.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 over- 把力量压在头顶之上。

items.example: Whelm supplies the covering image inside overwhelm.
items.exampleCN: whelm 提供词内「盖没」的意象。

items.example: Attaching the suffix to the verb gives overwhelming, the adjective of force.
items.exampleCN: 后缀加在动词上构成 overwhelming 这个表示力量之强的形容词。

items.example: Attaching the suffix to the adjective gives overwhelmingly, an adverb of margin.
items.exampleCN: 后缀加在形容词上构成表示压倒性程度的副词 overwhelmingly。

items.example: The prefix un- forms unwhelm, the reverse of being covered.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 un- 构成 unwhelm，表示不被盖没。

items.example: Overbear and overwhelm both open with the prefix over-.
items.exampleCN: overbear 与 overwhelm 同以 over- 开头。

items.example: Overpower swaps whelm for power, so it covers by strength.
items.exampleCN: overpower 把 whelm 换作 power，于是变成以力量钳制。

items.example: Overtake uses the same prefix for passing a line.
items.exampleCN: overtake 用同一前缀表示越过一条线。

items.example: Overload marks the burden sense of overwhelm simply.
items.exampleCN: overload 简单标出 overwhelm 里「负担」的那层义。

definition_zh: 工作过度；拼命干活；过重的工作量；使某人劳累过度；过度使用；（分词）过度劳累的；被用滥的
definition_en: to work, or to make someone work, more than is healthy or wise, and the excessive load of work that results from it
core_image: 同一张办公桌前，屏幕一直亮着，人却趴在键盘上，桌上摆满空咖啡杯
scene: 截止日是周五，周四整夜办公室的灯都没关，同事眯着眼睛还在敲键盘。The junior analyst overworked for three nights and finally fell asleep at her desk.
sceneCN: 这里 overwork 是「工作过度、拼命干活」（第 1 个义项：超过有益限度地工作）；句意为那位初级分析师连续三晚拼命工作，最后在办公桌旁睡着了。

pos.zh: 工作过度；使某人劳累过度；过度使用
过重的工作量；过度劳累；额外的工作
（分词）过度劳累的；被用滥的

derivatives.zh: 由本词加 -ed 分词后缀构成，义为「过度劳累的；被用滥的」
由本词加 -ing 名词后缀构成，义为「过度工作；过度使用」
由本词加 -er 后缀构成，义为「工作狂；过度工作的人」

senses.title: To work too much
senses.definition: to work more than is good or healthy for you
senses.definitionCN: 超过对身体或精神有益的限度而工作
senses.example: She overworked for weeks before the deadline.
senses.exampleCN: 截止日期之前，她连续几周拼命工作。
senses.why: The prefix over- means beyond a limit, so overwork is simply the act of working past the point where work should stop.
senses.whyCN: 前缀 over- 表示「超出限度」，所以 overwork 就是把工作推过本应停下的那条线的动作。

senses.title: Too much work as a burden
senses.definition: an amount of work that is too great for one person to do well
senses.definitionCN: 超出一个人所能胜任程度的工作量
senses.example: The whole team suffers from overwork.
senses.exampleCN: 整个团队都因工作量过重而受苦。
senses.why: The same amount that is too much for the body becomes the name of the excessive load itself, not only the act of doing it.
senses.whyCN: 对身体而言过多的那份量，不仅指做这件事的动作，也成了这份过量的负担本身的名称。

senses.title: To make someone work too hard
senses.definition: to make a person work so hard or so long that it harms them
senses.definitionCN: 使人过度劳累或超时工作，以致受到伤害
senses.example: The manager overworked the night staff again.
senses.exampleCN: 经理又一次让夜班员工劳累过度。
senses.why: The verb can turn outward: a boss becomes the one who pushes the limit onto somebody else.
senses.whyCN: 这个动词也可以向外指：老板成了把限度的压力施加到别人身上的那个人。

senses.title: To work a machine or material too hard
senses.definition: to use a machine or material so much that it wears out or fails
senses.definitionCN: 过度使用机器或材料，使其损耗或失效
senses.example: Do not overwork the engine on steep hills.
senses.exampleCN: 在陡坡上不要过度使用发动机。
senses.why: Work is energy spent, so anything that spends its energy past its limit is overworked, from an engine to an old tyre.
senses.whyCN: 工作就是消耗能量，凡是把能量消耗超过自身限度的东西都被称为 overworked，从发动机到旧轮胎都一样。

senses.title: To use a word or idea too much
senses.definition: to use a word, phrase, or theme so often that it loses its force
senses.definitionCN: 过频地使用某个词、成语或主题，使其失去力度
senses.example: Teenagers overwork the word literally.
senses.exampleCN: 青少年把 literally 这个词用得过滥了。
senses.why: The verb spreads from labour to any repeated effort: a word that is made to work too hard wears out just as a worker does.
senses.whyCN: 动词从体力劳动扩展到任何反复使用的努力：一个被逼着「过度劳动」的词，也会像工人一样被磨损。

senses.title: Overworked: exhausted by work
senses.definition: describing a person who is exhausted or stressed because they work too hard
senses.definitionCN: 形容因工作过多而疲惫、压力过大的人
senses.example: Overworked nurses are leaving the hospital.
senses.exampleCN: 过度劳累的护士正在离开这家医院。
senses.why: As a participle the verb turns into a state, so overworked names the visible result: a tired face and an empty tank.
senses.whyCN: 作分词时动词转为状态，如此 overworked 命名的就是看得见的结果：疲惫的脸和空掉的身体。

senses.title: Overworked: used until worn out
senses.definition: describing a machine, phrase, or image that has been used so often that it is worn, stale, or unreliable
senses.definitionCN: 形容机器、说法或图像因反复使用而磨损、陈旧或不可靠
senses.example: The report is full of overworked images of the city.
senses.exampleCN: 这份报告充满了对这座城市过于滥用的意象。
senses.why: The state sense splits again: things that are overworked end up either broken or simply boring from repetition.
senses.whyCN: 状态义再次分化：被过度使用的东西最终要么坏掉，要么因重复而变得乏味。

intro.en: Overwork is transparently English, a medieval compound of over and work that records the human habit of working past the limit.
intro.cn: overwork 是透明的英语合成词，由中古英语的 over 与 work 组合而成，记录了人把工作推过限度的习惯。

items.en: Work descends from Old English weorc and wyrcan, a word for doing and labouring; the over- element is the Old English prefix ofer, meaning above or beyond.
items.cn: work 源自古英语 weorc 与 wyrcan，表示「做事、劳动」；over- 则是古英语前缀 ofer，意为「在上方、超出」。

items.en: Over- had long combined with verbs and nouns in Middle English, as in overcharge and overflow, so the pattern was ready for a new member.
items.cn: 中古英语里 over- 早已与动词、名词大量组合，如 overcharge 与 overflow，这套构词模式已经准备好接纳新成员。

items.en: Put over plus work together and the meaning follows at once: work carried beyond the right measure. Many compounds of this shape follow the same logic.
items.cn: 把 over 与 work 拼在一起，意思立刻就出现：被带过适当尺度的工作；这一类 over- 复合词都遵循同样的逻辑。

items.en: The verb from this compound enters English somewhat later in the record than the simple nouns around it, and its exact first printing is uncertain.
items.cn: 由这一组合而来的动词在文献中出现得比周围的简单名词稍晚，确切的最早印本年代不确定。

items.en: Industrial labour gave the word its noun load sense, and from about the twentieth century it spread to engines and to overused words in journalism.
items.cn: 工业劳动给了它「过重工作量」的名词义，大约二十世纪起又扩展到发动机，以及新闻写作中被用滥的词语。

note.en: The look-alike group holds other over- compounds that share the same beyond-the-limit prefix; the near-meaning group holds words for the strain on the worker, the mood and the words that are worn out.
note.cn: 形近组收其他同样带「超出限度」前缀的 over- 复合词；近义组收描述工人疲倦、情绪低落与被磨坏用词的词。

entries.definition: To put more into a container than it can hold; the prefix carries the same too much idea.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「装得过满」，前缀 over- 携带同样的「过量」意象。

entries.definition: To put too much weight, work or information on someone or something.
entries.definitionCN: 动词或名词，义为「使超载、超负荷」，同样指某个承载者超出限度。

entries.definition: To fill a space with too many people, leaving no room to move comfortably.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「使过于拥挤」，人挤进空间超过它的承载量。

entries.definition: A state of being completely used up, the result of working or using something too much.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「精疲力竭、耗尽」，是过度工作或用力的结果状态。

entries.definition: A state of physical and emotional collapse caused by long-term overwork; newer and more psychological.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「职业倦怠、精力耗尽」，指长期过劳造成的身心崩溃，更偏心理层面。

entries.definition: Describing a phrase or idea used so often that it no longer feels fresh; overlaps with overworked in its word sense.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「陈腐的、用滥的」，与 overworked 的「用词过滥」义重叠，但只用于说法。

normalIntro.en: These hooks turn on the literal parts of the word: over- beyond the limit, plus work, plus the -ed ending that makes the state.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些记忆钩子都围绕构词本身：over- 表示超出限度，work 是工作，-ed 把动作变成状态。

normal.en: Over- means beyond the mark, exactly as in overflow, overdue and overload.
normal.cn: over- 意为「超出界限」，正如 overflow、overdue、overload 中的用法。

normal.en: Work plus over turns any job into too much work, so the compound means work past the healthy point.
normal.cn: work 加上 over，任何工作都变成过量工作，所以这个合成词意为超过健康程度的工作。

normal.en: Overworked with -ed describes the person, not the task: the tired face is overworked, the schedule is overloaded.
normal.cn: 带 -ed 的 overworked 描述的是人而不是任务：疲惫的脸是 overworked，而日程表是 overloaded。

normal.en: A word or an engine is overworked when it has been made to work too long and loses its sharpness.
normal.cn: 词语或发动机被逼着工作太久、失去锐度时，也可说 overworked。

normal.en: Compare overload: overload adds too much in one moment, overwork adds too many hours again and again.
normal.cn: 对比 overload：overload 是在一瞬间加得太多，overwork 是一次又一次地加上太多小时。

abstract.en: Picture the red line drawn on a gauge: work is the needle, and overwork is the needle pushed right past it.
abstract.cn: 想象仪表上画着一条红线：工作是指针，overwork 就是把指针推过红线。

abstract.en: Imagine a desk lamp still on at midnight and the chair empty, while the screen keeps scrolling.
abstract.cn: 想象午夜时分台灯还亮着，椅子空了，屏幕却还在自动滚动。

abstract.en: Think of a handle polished thin by too many hands: often used words are polished until they show no grain at all.
abstract.cn: 想象一个被太多手磨得发亮的把手：被频繁使用的词也是这样被磨到看不出纹理。

examples.en: Doctors warn that many young professionals overwork to the point of collapse.
examples.cn: 医生警告说，许多年轻职场人过度工作，已经到了崩溃的边缘。

examples.en: Overworked crews are more likely to make careless mistakes.
examples.cn: 过度劳累的工人更容易犯粗心的错误。

examples.en: By December the word innovation had become an overworked phrase in their ads.
examples.cn: 到了十二月，innovation 这个词在他们的广告里已经成了一个用滥的说法。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「欧弗沃克」——欧式的老板连轴转，非得再「弗」上一层，「沃克」一天走个没完：工作过度、拼命干活；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 古英语前缀 ofer「在上方、超出」+ 古英语 weorc「工作」，由词缀义直接合成：把工作推到超过限度的地方。over- 作为「过度」前缀在中古英语已见于 overcharge、overflow，overwork 沿用同一模式；确切首次书面记录年代不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Overwork starts from the act of working past the limit, then names the extra load, the pushing of that load onto others and onto machines, and finally the worn-out state in people and in words.
sensesIntro.cn: overwork 从「把工作做到超过限度」的动作出发，再指那份额外的负担、把负担压给他人和机器，最后指人和词语被磨到疲惫、陈旧的状态。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a needle pressed past the red line marked on a gauge, while the worker at the desk has fallen asleep.
core.cn: 核心意象：仪表上的指针被推过红线，而桌前的人已经累得睡着了。

branches.en: THE ACT: a person steps over the healthy limit in their own hours.
branches.cn: 动作线：一个人用自己的时间跨过健康的限度。

branches.en: THE LOAD: the excess becomes a burden, and the same verb turns outward onto staff.
branches.cn: 负担线：过量变成了负担，同一个动词也可以向外指向员工。

branches.en: THE MACHINE: the limit applies to engines, materials and anything that spends energy.
branches.cn: 机器线：这条限度同样适用于发动机、材料以及任何消耗能量的东西。

branches.en: THE WORD: a phrase made to work too hard wears out and goes stale.
branches.cn: 用词线：被逼着过度工作的说法会被磨旧、变得陈腐。

branches.en: THE STATE: the participle shows the result in the tired face of the worker.
branches.cn: 状态线：分词展示结果，显现在劳动者疲惫的脸上。

intro.en: Overwork is a native English compound: the prefix over- and the base work, extended by -ed, -ing and -er.
intro.cn: overwork 是英语本土复合词：前缀 over- 加上词基 work，再靠 -ed、-ing、-er 扩展词族。

latinIntro.en: Both halves are Germanic and there is no Latin core here, so this section lists only the English structure rather than Latin cognates.
latinIntro.cn: 两部分都属日耳曼语，本词没有拉丁核心词，因此这一部分只列英语构词结构，不列拉丁同源词。

items.example: The prefix sets the limit that the base word crosses.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀划出词基所跨越的那条限度。

items.example: Work is the activity that is pushed too far.
items.exampleCN: work 就是被推得过远的那项活动。

items.meaning: to work beyond a healthy limit
items.example: The compound joins prefix and base without a suffix.
items.exampleCN: 这个复合词由前缀和词基直接拼成，不加后缀。

items.example: The suffix forms overworked, tired from work.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀构成 overworked，表示因工作而疲惫。

items.example: The suffix forms overworking as the ongoing process.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀构成 overworking，表示持续的过程。

items.example: The suffix forms overworker, a person who works too much.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀构成 overworker，指工作过多的人。

items.example: Overflow shows the prefix with another base.
items.exampleCN: overflow 展示这个前缀与另一个词基的组合。

items.example: Overload is the closest sibling of overwork.
items.exampleCN: overload 是与 overwork 最接近的同构词。

items.example: Overdue keeps the same beyond-the-limit sense.
items.exampleCN: overdue 保留着同样的「超出限度」含义。

definition_zh: 猫头鹰；（像猫头鹰一样）严肃或聪慧的；夜猫子；常熬夜的人
definition_en: a night-hunting bird of prey with a large round face and big forward eyes, and by extension anyone who is wide awake late at night or wears a solemn, knowing look
core_image: 深夜里一对圆圆的黄眼睛一动不动，转过头来盯住你
scene: 谷仓的横梁上，一对圆眼睛在黑暗中慢慢转动，随即无声地扑向田埂。A barn owl drifted over the stubble and left the mice no warning at all.
sceneCN: 这里 owl 是「猫头鹰」（第 1 个义项：圆脸大眼、夜间活动的猛禽）；句意为一只仓鸮掠过麦茬地，给田鼠们连个预警都没有留下。

pos.zh: 猫头鹰；夜猫子；严肃或聪慧的人

collocations.zh: 大大的圆眼睛（像猫头鹰的眼睛）

derivatives.zh: 由本词加指小后缀 -let 构成，义为「小猫头鹰」
由本词加形容词后缀 -ish 构成，义为「像猫头鹰似的；神情严肃而聪敏的」
由 owlish 加副词后缀 -ly 构成，义为「一本正经地；瞪圆眼睛地」

senses.title: A night bird of prey with a round face
senses.definition: a bird of prey with a large round head, big forward-facing eyes, and a hooked beak, most active at night
senses.definitionCN: 一种猛禽，头大而圆，双眼大且朝前，喙呈钩状，多在夜间活动
senses.example: An owl sat on the fence posts and watched the field.
senses.exampleCN: 一只猫头鹰蹲在栅栏柱上注视着田野。
senses.why: The word has named the bird since Old English ule, and the wide eyes on a round face are the same image that gave it the name.
senses.whyCN: 这个词自中古英语之前的古英语时期 ule 起就指这只鸟，圆脸上那对大眼正是给它命名的同一个意象。

senses.title: Owl-like in behaviour: solemn or wise
senses.titleCN: （像猫头鹰一样）严肃的；聪慧的
senses.definition: used to describe a person who looks solemn, studious, or unusually wise, as owls are in old stories
senses.definitionCN: 形容人神情严肃、好学或显得格外有智慧，因为老故事里的猫头鹰总是一副懂很多的样子
senses.example: He watched the lecture with his round owl eyes.
senses.exampleCN: 他瞪着一双圆圆的、像猫头鹰一样的眼睛听讲座。
senses.why: Because owls stare for long, still moments, people read intelligence and seriousness into them, and the stare is compared to the bird itself.
senses.whyCN: 因为猫头鹰会一动不动地长时凝视，人们便从中读出智慧和严肃，这种凝视就被比作这只鸟本身。

senses.title: A person who stays up late
senses.titleCN: 夜间清醒的人；常熬夜的人
senses.definition: informal, a person who is lively and active at night and often stays up very late
senses.definitionCN: 口语用语，指夜间精力充沛、常常熬夜的人
senses.example: She is an owl and hardly sleeps before two.
senses.exampleCN: 她是个十足的夜猫子，凌晨两点前几乎不睡。
senses.why: Owls hunt in darkness and sleep in daylight, so calling a late watcher an owl borrows the timetable of the bird itself.
senses.whyCN: 猫头鹰在黑暗中捕猎、白天睡觉，把熬夜者叫作 owl，就是借用了这只鸟自己的作息表。

senses.title: Night owl: the habitual late worker
senses.titleCN: 夜猫子：习惯深夜活动的人
senses.definition: in the fixed phrase night owl, a person whose best working or thinking hours come after midnight
senses.definitionCN: 用于固定搭配 night owl，指最佳工作或思考时间在午夜之后的人
senses.example: My night owl habits are why the rota puts me on the late shift.
senses.exampleCN: 正因为我习惯做夜猫子，排班时总把我排在夜班。
senses.why: Alone, owl means the bird; the added night pins the comparison to a daily rhythm, a pattern rather than one late evening.
senses.whyCN: 单独用时 owl 指那只鸟；加上 night 就把这个比喻固定在一种日常节律上，指的是作息习惯而不是某一个熬夜的晚上。

senses.title: Owl of the species in compounds
senses.definition: in the names of species and kinds, such as barn owl, snowy owl, and eagle owl, the word identifies the bird family
senses.definitionCN: 在物种或类别名称中，如 barn owl、snowy owl、eagle owl，owl 标出这类鸟的科属
senses.example: A barn owl hunted along the edge of the marsh.
senses.exampleCN: 一只仓鸮沿着沼泽边缘捕猎。
senses.why: Naming kinds by a modifier plus owl is a very old habit, so the bird name works as the last element of compound names.
senses.whyCN: 用修饰语加 owl 来给种类命名是一种很古老的习惯，因此鸟名常作复合名称的最后一个成分。

intro.en: Owl is a very old Germanic bird name, brought to England by the Anglo-Saxons and unchanged in its core for more than a thousand years.
intro.cn: owl 是一个很古老的日耳曼语鸟名，由盎格鲁-撒克逊人带到英格兰，一千多年里核心含义几乎未变。

items.en: The word continues a Germanic form of uncertain shape, generally reconstructed with a *u and an l, close to modern Dutch uil and German Eule.
items.cn: 这个词延续着一个形态不确定的日耳曼语形式，一般认为重构为带 *u 与 l 的形式，与荷兰语 uil、德语 Eule 相近。

items.en: Old English ule is the recorded form without an initial w, and it already named the bird in the night-hunter sense.
items.cn: 古英语 ule 是有文献记录的形式，开头没有 w，当时已经指这种夜间捕猎的鸟。

items.en: Middle English spellings such as owle and oule add a glide after the long vowel; this is when the written w first appears.
items.cn: 中古英语拼作 owle、oule 等，在长元音后加了滑音，书面上的 w 就是从这时开始出现的。

items.en: The modern spelling owl and the sound /aʊl/ are fixed by about the seventeenth century; earlier pronunciation had a long o sound.
items.cn: 现代的拼写 owl 与读音 /aʊl/ 大约到十七世纪才固定下来，更早的读音中是长 o 音。

items.en: From the 19th century the word spreads to compounds such as barn owl, and to the standing comparison night owl for a late riser.
items.cn: 从十九世纪起，这个词扩展到 barn owl 等复合词，以及 night owl 这个比喻熬夜者的固定说法。

note.en: The look-alike group holds other bird names that look or sound close to owl; the near-meaning group holds other night-hunting birds and the people who are named after them.
note.cn: 形近组收拼写或读音与 owl 接近的其他鸟名；近义组收其他夜间捕猎的鸟以及以这类鸟比喻的人。

entries.definition: A large powerful bird of prey that hunts by day and shares the open-eyed hunting look.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「鹰」，白天捕猎的大型猛禽，同样带着瞪眼捕猎的神情；只是与 owl 同为短鸟名。

entries.definition: A small pointed tool for making holes in leather or wood; sounds nearly the same but is not a bird.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「锥子」，做皮具或木工打孔用的小尖工具；读音与 owl 几乎相同，但只是拼写相近，词源不同。

entries.definition: To be obliged to pay money or show gratitude; looks close in three letters but comes from another root entirely.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「欠、应归功于」，三个字母的写法相近，但只是拼写相近，词源不同。

entries.definition: A dusk-hunting bird with an endless churring song, another hunter that works after dark.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「夜鹰」，黄昏捕猎的鸟，整夜发出颤鸣，同样是黑暗中工作的一类猎手。

entries.definition: A flying mammal that hunts insects by night and takes the place of owls in many night-time scenes.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「蝙蝠」，夜间捕虫的飞行哺乳动物，在许多夜间场景中替代了猫头鹰的位置。

entries.definition: A bird that sings at dawn; as a person name it is the opposite of an owl, a morning person.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「云雀」，清晨鸣唱的鸟；用来指人时与夜猫子正好相反，指早起的人。

normalIntro.en: These hooks work with the real history of the word, the sound of its long vowel, and the everyday phrases it appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些记忆钩子借助这个词真实的历史、长元音的读音，以及它实际出现的日常搭配。

normal.en: The same old bird name survives in Dutch uil and German Eule, so owl sits in a very old family of bird words.
normal.cn: 这个古老的鸟名在荷兰语 uil 与德语 Eule 中延续下来，可见 owl 属于一个很古老的鸟名词族。

normal.en: Old English had ule without a w; the w in the spelling arrived in Middle English.
normal.cn: 古英语原作 ule，没有 w；拼写中的 w 是中古英语时期才出现的。

normal.en: Owlet is a baby owl and owlish means looking like one, both built with ordinary English endings.
normal.cn: owlet 是「小猫头鹰」，owlish 意为「像猫头鹰的」，两者都由普通英语词尾构成。

normal.en: A barn owl is named for its usual home in a barn, so the compound works like a house label.
normal.cn: barn owl（仓鸮）因常住在谷仓而得名，这个复合词就像一个「房屋地址」。

normal.en: Compare owl person and lark person: the owl works at night, the lark is up before sunrise.
normal.cn: 对比 owl 型与 lark 型的人：前者在夜里活动，后者日出前就起床。

abstract.en: Picture the head rotating almost all the way round without the body moving at all.
abstract.cn: 想象那只鸟的头几乎转了一整圈，身子却纹丝不动。

abstract.en: Imagine two round yellow eyes in a dark barn, both fixed on you at once.
abstract.cn: 想象漆黑谷仓里一对圆圆的黄眼睛，同时定定地望着你。

abstract.en: Think of the clock talking to the bird of midnight: the bird of midnight is owl.
abstract.cn: 想象一只钟对午夜的鸟说话：午夜的鸟就是 owl。

examples.en: Owls are protected because they keep mouse numbers down.
examples.cn: 猫头鹰受到保护，因为它们能控制老鼠的数量。

examples.en: I became a real owl in my final year, studying till three most nights.
examples.cn: 到了最后一年，我成了真正的夜猫子，大多数晚上都学到三点。

examples.en: She raised one eyebrow and gave him a long owl look.
examples.cn: 她挑起一边眉毛，用猫头鹰般的长长注视打量了他一阵。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「凹乌」——脸上一个「凹」下去的圆盘，一声「乌」叫掠过夜空：猫头鹰；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 古英语 ule「猫头鹰」，下接形态不确定的日耳曼语重构形式（一般认为带 *u 与 l），与荷兰语 uil、德语 Eule 同源；中古英语拼作 owle 时在长元音后增入滑音 w，形成今天的 owl。

sensesIntro.en: Owl begins with the bird itself, extends to the solemn or knowing look the bird wears in stories, then to people who share its timetable and to the compound names built on it.
sensesIntro.cn: owl 先指这只鸟本身，再扩展到故事里它那副严肃而通晓的神情，然后指与它作息相仿的人，以及由它构成的种类名称。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two round yellow eyes that fix on you in the dark and a silent glide over the field.
core.cn: 核心意象：黑暗中一对圆圆的黄眼睛定定盯住你，随后无声地掠过田野。

branches.en: THE BIRD: the concrete hunter, first and always the centre of the word.
branches.cn: 鸟本身：具体的猎手，始终是这个词的中心。

branches.en: THE FACE: a long, still stare makes a person seem owl-like and wise.
branches.cn: 神情线：长久的凝视让人显得像猫头鹰，也显得有智慧。

branches.en: THE CLOCK: the bird works in darkness, so late people inherit its role.
branches.cn: 作息线：这只鸟在黑暗中工作，于是熬夜的人继承了它的角色。

branches.en: THE NAMES: modifiers plus owl label each kind of the family.
branches.cn: 名称线：修饰语加上 owl，为这一科里的每个种类贴上标签。

branches.en: One bird name supports both the loose use and the exact scientific-style use.
branches.cn: 同一个鸟名同时支撑泛用与近似科学式精确称呼两种用法。

intro.en: Owl is a short Germanic root on its own; the English family grows from it with the endings -let, -ish and -ly.
intro.cn: owl 本身是一个简短的日耳曼语词根；英语词族靠 -let、-ish、-ly 等词尾从它生长出来。

latinIntro.en: Owl has no Latin origin, so no Latin cognate is listed; the Latin bird name for this family is strix, which came into scientific use separately.
latinIntro.cn: owl 并非源自拉丁语，因此不列拉丁同源词；拉丁语把这类鸟称作 strix，这个词是另外进入科学用语的。

items.example: The base noun has stayed almost unchanged for a millennium.
items.exampleCN: 这个词基本身一千年来几乎没变。

items.example: The suffix forms owlet for a young owl.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀构成 owlet，指幼小的猫头鹰。

items.example: Owlet keeps the bird and adds smallness.
items.exampleCN: owlet 保留鸟义，再添上「小」的意思。

items.example: The suffix forms the adjective owlish.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀构成形容词 owlish。

items.meaning: like an owl; solemn and studious
items.meaningCN: 像猫头鹰的；严肃好学的
items.example: Owlish describes both the face and the manner.
items.exampleCN: owlish 既可描述面孔，也可描述神态。

items.example: The suffix forms the adverb owlishly.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀构成副词 owlishly。

items.meaning: a person active late at night
items.example: The compound does not describe a real bird.
items.exampleCN: 这个复合短语并不指真的鸟。

items.meaning: a pale owl often found in barns
items.example: Here the first word names its usual home.
items.exampleCN: 这里的第一个词标出它常住的处所。

definition_zh: 氧化物；氧化物层；（二氧化碳、一氧化碳等复合名称中的）二氧化物、一氧化物；氧化膜
definition_en: a chemical compound in which oxygen is joined to one other element, and by extension a layer or material made of such a compound
core_image: 新切开的铁块一夜之间蒙上一层红褐色的壳
scene: 仓库角落的钢板上，原本银白的切面，隔夜便爬满一层红褐色的薄壳。Those red-brown flakes on the nail heads are an oxide that formed overnight.
sceneCN: 这里 oxide 是「氧化物、氧化层」（第 1 个义项：氧与另一种元素化合成的化合物）；句意为钉头上那些红褐色的碎屑是一夜之间形成的氧化物。

pos.zh: 氧化物；氧化层、氧化膜；（作修饰语）氧化物的

derivatives.zh: 本词的复数形式，义为「多种氧化物」
由本词加动词后缀 -ize 构成，义为「使氧化；（金属）生锈」
由 oxidize 加 -ation 构成，义为「氧化作用、被氧化的过程」
由 di-（二）加本词构成，义为「二氧化物」，如 carbon dioxide

senses.title: A compound of oxygen and one other element
senses.definition: a chemical compound in which oxygen is combined with one other element, such as iron oxide or zinc oxide
senses.definitionCN: 氧与另一种元素化合成的化合物，如氧化铁或氧化锌
senses.example: Iron oxide gives the desert its red colour.
senses.exampleCN: 氧化铁让沙漠泛出红色。
senses.why: The -ide ending, modelled on oxide itself, marks a binary compound, and ox- points to the partner: oxygen. An oxide is oxygen plus one other element, nothing else.
senses.whyCN: 后缀 -ide 仿照 oxide 本身而来，标记二元化合物，而 ox- 指出搭档是氧；氧化物就是氧加上另一种元素，别的不加。

senses.title: Carbon dioxide and carbon monoxide
senses.titleCN: （复合名称中的）二氧化物、一氧化物
senses.definition: in compound names such as carbon dioxide and carbon monoxide, the word tells how many oxygen atoms share the molecule and what they are attached to
senses.definitionCN: 在 carbon dioxide、carbon monoxide 这类复合名称中，指出分子里有多少个氧原子，以及它们附着在什么元素上
senses.example: Carbon dioxide and carbon monoxide are both oxides of carbon.
senses.exampleCN: 二氧化碳与一氧化碳都是碳的氧化物。
senses.why: Once the ending names a class, prefixes can count the oxygens, and a modifier can name the partner, giving a naming system rather than a single word.
senses.whyCN: 当词尾命名一个类别之后，前缀就能数氧原子的个数，修饰语则说出搭档元素，于是词变成一套命名系统，而不只是一个孤立的词。

senses.title: A thin film formed by oxidation
senses.titleCN: 氧化层；身上的氧化物薄膜
senses.definition: a thin layer of oxide that forms on the surface of a metal, often protecting it or discolouring it
senses.definitionCN: 金属表面形成的一层很薄的氧化物，常起保护作用或使表面变色
senses.example: The aluminium panel wears a dull grey oxide.
senses.exampleCN: 这块铝板表面长着一层暗灰色的氧化层。
senses.why: The general compound becomes the concrete crust you can see and touch: the oxide that has already grown on a surface.
senses.whyCN: 一般意义上的化合物落实为看得见摸得着的一层壳：已经长在表面上的那层氧化物。

senses.title: An oxide as a pigment or material
senses.definition: an oxide used on purpose as a pigment, a coating, or an industrial material, such as zinc oxide in paint
senses.definitionCN: 有意用作颜料、涂层或工业材料的氧化物，如涂料中的氧化锌
senses.example: Zinc oxide keeps the artists white work from yellowing.
senses.exampleCN: 氧化锌能防止画家的白色作品发黄。
senses.why: The same powder on the shelf has a job, so the word can point at the substance as something chosen, sold and used, not only a product of chemistry.
senses.whyCN: 同样一堆粉料在架上自有用途，所以这个词也可指被挑选、出售和使用的物质，而不只是化学反应的产物。

senses.title: Oxide as a qualifier in technical compounds
senses.definition: used as the first element in technical names such as oxide film, oxide layer, and oxide ore, naming something made of or based on oxide
senses.definitionCN: 作为技术名词的第一个成分，如 oxide film、oxide layer、oxide ore，指由氧化物构成或以其为基础的东西
senses.example: The oxide layer makes the steel harder to weld.
senses.exampleCN: 这层氧化膜让钢更难焊接。
senses.why: When a whole class of substances needs a label, the class name moves in front of another noun and works like an adjective.
senses.whyCN: 当一整类物质需要标签时，类名就移到另一个名词前面，充当形容词。

intro.en: Oxide began as a made-up name at the edge of the eighteenth century, when chemists needed one word for oxygen joined to something else. Its partner card -ide spread from it to hundreds of compounds.
intro.cn: oxide 是十八世纪末由化学家造出的名字，用于给「氧与某物化合」这件事一个统一的词；它借来的 -ide 词尾后来扩散到数百种化合物。

items.en: The ox- part goes back to Greek oxys, sharp or acute, which already sat inside French oxygène because the gas was believed to give the sharp taste to acids.
items.cn: ox- 部分源自希腊语 oxys「尖锐、锐利」，它早已出现在法语 oxygène 中，因为当时认为这种气体是酸产生尖锐味道的原因。

items.en: French chemists coined oxygène as a noun for the gas, and compounds with it were soon built from the same stem with the ending -ide, as in oxide.
items.cn: 法国化学家在十八世纪八零年代造出 oxygène 一词指这种气体，随后很快用同一词干加 -ide 词尾构成氧化物，即 oxide。

items.en: English chemistry adopts oxide near the end of the eighteenth century, and within a generation it is the standard name for a compound of oxygen with another element.
items.cn: 英语化学界在十八世纪末采纳了 oxide，一代人之内它就成为「氧与另一元素化合物」的标准名称。

items.en: As gases like carbon dioxide and carbon monoxide became everyday scientific terms, oxide as the closing card of compound names spread into technical English.
items.cn: 随着 carbon dioxide、carbon monoxide 等气体成为日常科学术语，oxide 作为复合名称的收尾词在技术英语中广泛流传。

items.en: Modern technology adds oxide layer, oxide ore and oxide film, and everyday English keeps the word in rust, white paint and greenhouse talk.
items.cn: 现代技术又加入 oxide layer、oxide ore、oxide film 等说法，日常英语则把这个词留在铁锈、白漆与温室效应的话题里。

note.en: The look-alike group holds names built on the Greek sharp stem or on the -ide ending, which share shape rather than meaning; the near-meaning group holds other words that go with oxygen, metals and rust.
note.cn: 形近组收建在希腊「尖锐」词干或 -ide 词尾上的名称，它们共享形式而非意义；近义组收与氧、金属和铁锈相关的词。

entries.definition: The gas itself, the element every oxide contains; its name shares the oxy- stem but ends differently.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「氧」，是每种氧化物都含有的元素，名称共享 oxy- 词干，但词尾不同。

entries.definition: A compound with two oxygen atoms, as in carbon dioxide; built directly from oxide with the prefix di-.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「二氧化物」，如二氧化碳，由 oxide 直接加前缀 di- 构成。

entries.definition: To combine with oxygen or lose electrons; the verb that turns metal into oxide.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「使氧化、生锈」，是把金属变成氧化物的那个动作。

entries.definition: The red-brown flaky coating on iron, which is one everyday oxide made visible.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「铁锈」，铁表面红褐色易剥落的薄层，正是一种看得见的氧化物。

entries.definition: A compound of chlorine with another element; chloride is the same -ide pattern with another element card at the front.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「氯化物」，氯与另一元素化合的化合物，用的是同样的 -ide 模式，只是把开头的元素换成氯。

entries.definition: The process of combining with oxygen, as opposed to the compound that results from it.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「氧化作用」，指与氧结合的过程，与作为结果的化合物相对。

normalIntro.en: These hooks stay with the word history and the naming habits of chemistry, so they cannot lead you to a false root.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子围绕真实的词史与化学命名习惯，不会把你带到错误的词根上。

normal.en: The -ide in oxide is now a general ending for compounds, so chloride, bromide and sulphide follow the same card.
normal.cn: oxide 里的 -ide 如今已是化合物通用的词尾，chloride、bromide、sulphide 都沿用同一张牌。

normal.en: The ox- part comes from Greek oxys, sharp, the same stem that built oxygen, and it never comes from the animal ox.
normal.cn: ox- 部分来自希腊语 oxys「尖锐」，与 oxygen 共用词干，别把它和牛（ox）联系起来。

normal.en: Oxide means oxygen plus one other element, so dioxide adds one more oxygen and monoxide takes it away.
normal.cn: oxide 意为氧加另一种元素，dioxide 多一个氧，monoxide 少一个氧。

normal.en: Oxidize is the verb, oxidation is the process, oxide is the substance that is left.
normal.cn: oxidize 是动词，oxidation 是过程，oxide 是留下的那种物质。

normal.en: Rust is only iron oxide, so the word already hides in your everyday English.
normal.cn: 铁锈不过是氧化铁，所以这个词早已藏在你日常英语里了。

abstract.en: Picture a scratch of fresh metal that turns the colour of dried blood by morning.
abstract.cn: 想象一道崭新金属的划痕，到早晨已变成干血一样的颜色。

abstract.en: Imagine the word oxide as a label card hanging off every atom that has grabbed its own oxygen.
abstract.cn: 想象 oxide 是一张小标签，挂在每个抓到氧原子的原子上。

abstract.en: Think of the -ide ending as a hook that catches whatever element stands in front of it.
abstract.cn: 把 -ide 词尾想成一只钩子，钩住站在它前面的那个元素名称。

examples.en: The lab heats the metal oxide to recover pure metal.
examples.cn: 实验室加热金属氧化物，以回收纯金属。

examples.en: A thin oxide film on the copper hides its shine.
examples.cn: 铜表面的一层薄氧化膜盖住了它的光泽。

examples.en: Dust from the quarry carries both silicon and iron oxides into the river.
examples.cn: 采石场的粉尘把硅和铁的氧化物一并带进了河里。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「奥克赛德」——像运动员奥克在赛道上把氧牢牢扣住：氧化物、氧化层；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: ox- 源自希腊语 oxys「尖锐」（经由法语 oxygène，因当时认为氧是酸中尖锐味道的来源）+ 化学词尾 -ide（是 oxide 本身带动了这类词尾的流传）。也就是说，oxide 由法语 oxygène 的同一词干加 -ide 构成，并非来自拉丁语。

sensesIntro.en: Oxide runs from the general chemical class, through countable compound names and the visible skin on metal, to the substance sold as a material and the qualifier in technical compounds.
sensesIntro.cn: oxide 从一般化学类别出发，经过可数的复合名称和金属表面看得见的那层壳，再到当作材料出售的物质，以及技术名词前作修饰语的位置。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: freshly cut metal grows a red-brown skin overnight.
core.cn: 核心意象：新切开的金属一夜之间长出一层红褐色的皮。

branches.en: THE CLASS: one broad category covers every compound of oxygen with one other element.
branches.cn: 类别线：一个宽泛类别覆盖氧与另一种元素的全部化合物。

branches.en: THE NAMES: prefixes count the oxygen atoms and modifiers name the partner.
branches.cn: 命名线：前缀数氧原子的个数，修饰语说出搭档元素。

branches.en: THE SKIN: the compound as something that has already formed on a surface.
branches.cn: 表层线：化合物作为已经在表面上形成的东西出现。

branches.en: THE MATERIAL: the same reaction product used and sold on purpose.
branches.cn: 材料线：同样的反应产物被有意使用和出售。

branches.en: THE LABEL: the class name becomes a modifier in oxide layer, oxide ore and oxide film.
branches.cn: 标签线：类名变成 oxide layer、oxide ore、oxide film 中的修饰语。

intro.en: Oxide is a word of Greek root and French coinage, and its -ide ending has become one of the most productive cards in chemistry.
intro.cn: oxide 由希腊词根与法语造词合成，它的 -ide 词尾已成为化学中最能产的构词成分之一。

latinIntro.en: The word does not come from Latin; oxy- is Greek and -ide was modelled on the French-made name, so this list shows the Greek root and the chemistry endings instead of Latin cognates.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词并非来自拉丁语：oxy- 是希腊语词干，-ide 是仿照法语造出的名称而来，因此这里列出希腊词根与化学生词词尾，不列拉丁同源词。

items.example: The Greek root names sharpness and is shared with oxygen.
items.exampleCN: 这个希腊词根意为「尖锐」，与 oxygen 共用。

items.meaningCN: 化合物词尾，表示与另一种元素化合
items.example: The suffix has become the general end of compound names.

items.meaning: a compound with two oxygen atoms

senses.title: An edible bivalve shellfish
senses.definition: a rough-shelled sea creature with a soft body, often eaten as food
senses.definitionCN: 一种壳面粗糙、身体柔软的海生双壳动物，常作食物
senses.example: He ordered a dozen oysters for dinner.
senses.exampleCN: 他晚餐点了十二只牡蛎。
senses.why: The Greek noun ostreon names a hard shell, so the creature was first known by its tough outside.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语名词指「坚硬的壳」，所以这种生物最早是以它坚硬的外壳得名的。

senses.title: A source of pearls
senses.definition: the shellfish in whose shell a pearl may form around an irritating grain
senses.definitionCN: 贝壳内可能围绕刺激物形成珍珠的贝类
senses.example: Divers searched the reef for oysters that held pearls.
senses.exampleCN: 潜水员在礁石间寻找含珍珠的牡蛎。
senses.why: Because a pearl grows inside a closed shell, the same animal also stands for hidden treasure.
senses.whyCN: 珍珠在紧闭的贝壳里长成，所以这种动物也代表藏在里面的珍宝。

senses.title: A silent, close-mouthed person
senses.titleCN: 沉默寡言的人；嘴紧的人
senses.definition: a person who keeps silent or does not share secrets
senses.definitionCN: 沉默不语或不肯泄露秘密的人
senses.example: When they asked about the plan, he became an oyster.
senses.exampleCN: 他们问起计划时，他就闭口不言了。
senses.why: A shut oyster reveals nothing, so the word was borrowed for a person who guards words like a closed shell.
senses.whyCN: 合上的牡蛎什么也不露，于是这个词被借来形容把话像壳一样守住的人。

senses.title: Something one may freely take
senses.titleCN: 可随意获取之物；囊中之物
senses.definition: a thing or opportunity that lies open for a person to enjoy or use
senses.definitionCN: 摆在那里任人享用或利用的东西或机会
senses.example: With a good degree, the world becomes an oyster to you.
senses.exampleCN: 有了好学位，世界就成了任你取用的东西。
senses.why: A shell can be opened with effort, so what lies inside comes to mean a reward one is free to take.
senses.whyCN: 壳努力撬开就能取出里面的东西，所以壳内的内容被引申为可以自由取得的回报。

senses.title: The meat of the shellfish
senses.definition: the soft flesh inside the shell, eaten raw or cooked
senses.definitionCN: 壳内柔软的可食之肉，生食或烹食
senses.example: The sauce is made with fresh oysters and lemon.
senses.exampleCN: 这种酱汁是用新鲜蚝肉和柠檬做的。
senses.why: Metonymy lets the container name the food, so the word also points to the flesh itself.
senses.whyCN: 借代让容器代替内容，所以这个词也指壳里的肉本身。

senses.title: A grey-brown oyster colour
senses.definition: a pale greyish brown colour like the outside of an oyster shell
senses.definitionCN: 像牡蛎壳外表那样的浅灰褐色
senses.example: She painted the walls a soft oyster white.
senses.exampleCN: 她把墙刷成了柔和的牡蛎白。
senses.why: Colours are often named after familiar objects, and the rough shell gave English an oyster shade.
senses.whyCN: 颜色常以常见物品命名，粗糙的贝壳也就给英语带来了一种牡蛎色。

senses.title: A small amount of money
senses.definition: a small sum of money, as in the phrase oyster money
senses.definitionCN: 一小笔钱，见于「oyster money」这类说法
senses.example: The old sailor set aside his oyster money in a tin.
senses.exampleCN: 老水手把小笔积蓄放进一个铁盒里。
senses.why: Oyster fishermen were paid in small amounts, so a modest sum of cash took the shellfish name.
senses.whyCN: 采蚝人按小额结算工钱，于是一小笔现钱也借用了这种贝类的名字。

senses.title: A quiet, unopened thing
senses.titleCN: 不开口的东西；紧闭之物
senses.definition: anything that stays closed or shows nothing on the surface
senses.definitionCN: 保持闭合或表面不露声色的任何东西
senses.example: The town was an oyster of old stories, closed to strangers.
senses.exampleCN: 这座小镇是一段封存的老故事，对陌生人紧闭。
senses.why: The shell image stretches to any sealed thing, so an oyster becomes a closed book or a silent place.
senses.whyCN: 贝壳的形象可以推及一切封闭之物，于是一只牡蛎就成了打不开的书或沉默的地方。

intro.en: Oyster comes through Old French oistre from Latin ostrea, which borrowed Greek ostreon, a word for the hard-shelled oyster.
intro.cn: oyster 经古法语 oistre 来自拉丁语 ostrea，而拉丁语又借自希腊语 ostreon，这个希腊词指硬壳的牡蛎。

items.en: Ostreon names the oyster and is linked to the idea of a hard shell or bone.
items.cn: ostreon 指牡蛎，一般认为与「硬壳、骨骼」的概念有关。

items.en: Ostrea is the Latin form of the word, and it is the source of many later names.
items.cn: ostrea 是这个词的拉丁语形式，也是后世许多名称的来源。

items.en: Related forms such as ostricen appear early in English, inside the Old English period.
items.cn: 相关形式如 ostricen 在古英语时期就已出现。

items.en: Oistre brings the word again through Norman French.
items.cn: oistre 又把这个词经由诺曼法语带入英语。

items.en: Oystre or oister settles into English as a common seaside word.
items.cn: oystre 或 oister 在中古英语中定型为常见的海边用词。

items.en: Oyster is standard by the 1600s, and its idioms spread into everyday speech.
items.cn: 到十七世纪 oyster 已成为标准拼写，相关习语也进入日常口语。

note.en: Oyster belongs to the shellfish family, and its look-alikes rest on the same Latin ostrea and the same closed shell.
note.cn: oyster 属于贝类词族，形近词都立在同一个拉丁词和「紧闭的壳」这个意象上。

normalIntro.en: Oyster is the shellfish of the hard shell: it keeps its soft inside and its riches shut away.
normalIntro.cn: oyster 是「硬壳贝」：柔软的里面和它的宝贝都被壳关着。

normal.en: The spelling oy-ster keeps two chunks, oy and ster, and the ster ending also shows in lobster.
normal.cn: 拼写可拆成 oy 和 ster 两截，结尾 ster 也出现在 lobster 里。

normal.en: A pearl grows inside an oyster, so the shell holds a hidden treasure.
normal.cn: 珍珠在牡蛎里长大，所以壳里藏着宝物。

normal.en: Oyster bed and oyster farm both describe places where oysters are raised.
normal.cn: oyster bed 与 oyster farm 都是养蚝的地方。

normal.en: To be as silent as an oyster means to say nothing at all.
normal.cn: 像牡蛎一样沉默，就是一句话也不说。

normal.en: Latin ostrea and Greek ostreon are the older names behind the English word.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 ostrea 与希腊语 ostreon 是英语词背后的古老名字。

abstract.en: Picture a rough shell on the stall, pried open with a short knife.
abstract.cn: 想象摊位上一只粗糙的壳，被一把小刀撬开。

abstract.en: Imagine a small round pearl glowing in the dark inside the shell.
abstract.cn: 想象壳内暗处一颗圆润的珍珠在发亮。

abstract.en: See a person pressing their lips shut, with a shell for a face.
abstract.cn: 想象一个人抿紧嘴唇，脸像一只壳。

examples.en: The restaurant serves fresh oysters with lemon and bread.
examples.cn: 这家餐厅供应配柠檬和面包的新鲜牡蛎。

examples.en: A pearl forms when a grain of sand irritates an oyster.
examples.cn: 当一粒沙刺激牡蛎时，珍珠就形成了。

examples.en: After the exam results came out, the world was his oyster.
examples.cn: 考试成绩公布后，整个世界都在他掌握之中。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「奥伊斯特」——海边小摊吆喝着「蚝伊」，壳一撬就吃；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 希腊语 ostreon（硬壳的牡蛎）→ 拉丁语 ostrea → 古法语 oistre → 中古英语 oystre → 现代英语 oyster；核心义「硬壳包着的软体海贝」。

sensesIntro.en: Oyster begins as the hard-shelled shellfish, grows into the pearl source and the meat, then turns figurative: a closed person, a free reward, a colour, and small money.
sensesIntro.cn: oyster 从硬壳贝类出发，长出「珍珠来源」「蚝肉」的意义，再转向比喻义：闭嘴的人、任取的机会、一种颜色和小额的钱。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a rough grey shell clamped shut around soft flesh.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只灰白粗糙的壳紧紧合着，裹住柔软的肉。

branches.en: The shellfish itself is the everyday sense.
branches.cn: 这种贝类本身是日常义项。

branches.en: The pearl and the flesh are what the closed shell holds.
branches.cn: 珍珠与肉是紧闭的壳里所盛的东西。

branches.en: A shut shell becomes a silent person, and an opened shell becomes a free reward.
branches.cn: 合上的壳变成沉默的人，撬开的壳变成可任取的回报。

branches.en: The colour sense borrows the look of the outer shell.
branches.cn: 颜色义借用了外壳的外观。

branches.en: The shellfish name spreads to small coin and to any closed thing.
branches.cn: 这种贝类的名字扩展到小笔钱与一切封闭之物。

intro.en: Oyster is mostly a borrowed base word, with English compounds like oysterman built by adding man or woman.
intro.cn: oyster 基本是借入的基础词，英语靠加 man、woman 等构成 oysterman 一类复合词。

latinIntro.en: Latin ostrea and its Greek source ostreon give the oyster word family across Europe.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 ostrea 及其希腊来源 ostreon 为欧洲各语言提供了牡蛎词族。

items.example: Ostreon is the oldest form of the word family.
items.exampleCN: ostreon 是这个词族最古老的形式。

items.example: Latin ostrea was borrowed from Greek.
items.exampleCN: 拉丁语 ostrea 借自希腊语。

items.example: Oistre is the Old French form.
items.exampleCN: oistre 是古法语形式。

items.example: Oyster is standard in modern English.
items.exampleCN: oyster 是现代英语的标准写法。

items.example: The suffix -s makes oysters.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -s 构成 oysters。

items.example: The form -man makes oysterman.
items.exampleCN: 构词成分 -man 构成 oysterman。

items.example: The suffix -ing makes oystering.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ing 构成 oystering。

items.example: This word comes from ostrakon, a shell used for voting, not from the oyster itself.
items.exampleCN: 这个词来自用于投票的陶片，并不是从牡蛎本身来的。

definition_zh: 臭氧；臭氧层；清新空气；海边清冽的空气
definition_en: a form of oxygen with a sharp smell that forms a thin layer high in the sky and shields the earth from harmful rays
core_image: 一层淡蓝色的薄雾高高罩在地球上方，把烈日挡在外面
scene: 雷雨过后，空气里飘着一股刺鼻又清凉的气味。After the thunderstorm, the air carried a sharp, clean ozone smell.
