senses.title: A sharp-smelling form of oxygen
senses.definition: a pale blue gas made of three oxygen atoms, with a strong clean smell
senses.definitionCN: 由三个氧原子组成的淡蓝色气体，带有强烈的清新气味
senses.example: Lightning can turn some oxygen into ozone.
senses.exampleCN: 闪电能把一部分氧气变成臭氧。
senses.why: The Greek verb ozein means to smell, so the gas was named for the sharp odour it gives off.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语动词意为「散发气味」，所以这种气体因它刺鼻的气味而得名。

senses.title: The protective layer high in the sky
senses.definition: the layer of ozone in the upper atmosphere that blocks harmful rays from the sun
senses.definitionCN: 大气上层阻挡太阳有害射线的臭氧层
senses.example: The ozone layer protects us from harmful sun rays.
senses.exampleCN: 臭氧层保护我们免受有害太阳射线的伤害。
senses.why: Because the gas gathers into a thin high layer, the word comes to name that whole shield.
senses.whyCN: 这种气体在高空聚成薄薄一层，于是这个词也指整层屏障。

senses.title: Fresh, clean air
senses.definition: air that feels fresh and clean, especially after a storm or by the sea
senses.definitionCN: 尤指雷雨之后或海边那种清新洁净的空气
senses.example: We opened the window to let in the fresh ozone.
senses.exampleCN: 我们打开窗户，让清新的空气进来。
senses.why: The sea air was once thought to carry ozone, so a bracing breeze took the name of the gas.
senses.whyCN: 人们曾以为海边空气含有臭氧，于是清冽的海风就借用了这种气体的名字。

senses.title: Ozone in the lower air as a pollutant
senses.definition: ozone near the ground, formed in sunlight, that harms lungs and plants
senses.definitionCN: 在阳光下于近地面生成的臭氧，会损害肺与植物
senses.example: Traffic fumes help create ozone pollution in summer cities.
senses.exampleCN: 汽车尾气会助长夏季城市的臭氧污染。
senses.why: High ozone means different things, so the word is marked by place: good high up, harmful down low.
senses.whyCN: 同一个臭氧在高空和低处意义不同，所以这个词用位置来区分：高处是好事，低处是害处。

senses.title: A sharp, electric smell
senses.titleCN: 臭氧味；刺鼻的清新气味
senses.definition: a smell like lightning or burnt air that stings the nose
senses.definitionCN: 像雷电或烧过的空气那样刺鼻的气味
senses.example: There was a strong smell of ozone in the air after the strike.
senses.exampleCN: 雷击之后空气里有一股浓烈的刺鼻气味。
senses.why: The Greek root gives smelling power, so the word can name the odour itself rather than the gas.
senses.whyCN: 希腊词根带有「嗅」的意思，所以这个词也能直接指气味本身，而不只是气体。

senses.title: Something refreshing and bracing
senses.titleCN: 清爽振奋之感；清新振奋
senses.definition: a quality of air or energy that wakes a person up
senses.definitionCN: 让空气或精神令人为之一振的清爽感
senses.example: The early run gave her a real ozone feeling.
senses.exampleCN: 清晨的跑步给了她一种真正清爽振奋的感觉。
senses.why: From sea air the word drifts to any quality that feels clean and energising.
senses.whyCN: 从海边空气出发，这个词延伸到任何让人觉得洁净、提神的感觉。

senses.title: Ozone used for cleaning
senses.definition: ozone used in water treatment and as a disinfectant because it kills microbes
senses.definitionCN: 用于水处理与消毒、能杀灭微生物的臭氧
senses.example: The plant uses ozone to clean the water supply.
senses.exampleCN: 这家工厂用臭氧净化供水。
senses.why: When chemists learned that ozone kills germs, the word extended to the gas as a working tool.
senses.whyCN: 当化学家发现臭氧能杀菌时，这个词就延伸为作为一种工作工具的臭氧。

senses.title: Ozone known as a pollutant in smog
senses.definition: the ozone found in city smog that makes some breathing hard
senses.definitionCN: 城市烟雾中的臭氧，使一些人呼吸困难
senses.example: The city posted an ozone warning on hot sunny days.
senses.exampleCN: 在炎热晴朗的日子，该市发布了臭氧预警。
senses.why: The same gas that shields at the top of the sky becomes a hazard in a smoggy street.
senses.whyCN: 这种在高空充当防护罩的气体，在烟雾弥漫的街道上却成了危害。

intro.en: Ozone was coined in the 1800s from the Greek verb ozein, to smell, because the gas has a sharp odour.
intro.cn: ozone 在十九世纪依据希腊语动词「嗅」造出，因为这种气体有刺鼻气味；一般认为由德国化学家舍恩拜因命名。

items.en: Ozein means to smell or give off an odour, and ozo means I smell.
items.cn: ozein 意为嗅、散发气味，ozo 意为「我闻」。

items.en: A German chemist names the newly found gas ozon after its smell.
items.cn: 一般认为，由德国化学家根据气味把新发现的气体命名为 ozon。

items.en: The French form ozone spreads the name through European science.
items.cn: 法语形式 ozone 在欧洲科学界扩展了这个名称。

items.en: English takes the word ozone for the gas and its smell.
items.cn: 英语借入 ozone，指这种气体及其气味。

items.en: From the 1900s, scientists use ozone for the layer high in the sky.
items.cn: 从二十世纪起，科学家用 ozone 指高空的大气层。

items.en: The ozone layer and ozone hole become everyday news words.
items.cn: 臭氧层与臭氧空洞成为日常新闻用词。

note.en: Ozone sits among chemical words built on the same Greek smell root, next to its companion gases.
note.cn: ozone 立在希腊语「嗅」词根上，属于化学词族，并与同类气体并列。

entries.definition: of or like ozone
entries.definitionCN: 臭氧的；像臭氧的

entries.definition: to treat something with ozone
entries.definitionCN: 用臭氧处理某物

entries.definition: the layer of the atmosphere rich in ozone
entries.definitionCN: 臭氧层；富含臭氧的大气层

entries.definition: the gas we breathe, of which ozone is a form
entries.definitionCN: 我们呼吸的氧气，臭氧是它的一种同素异形体

entries.definition: a dark haze of smoke and fog in cities
entries.definitionCN: 城市中烟与雾混成的污浊雾气

entries.definition: the whole body of air around a planet
entries.definitionCN: 环绕行星的全部空气

normalIntro.en: Ozone is a gas of three oxygen atoms and a sharp smell: z and n mark the odour and the way it is made.
normalIntro.cn: ozone 是三个氧原子组成的刺鼻气体：z 与 n 帮你记住它的气味和造法。

normal.en: The prefix oz- comes from Greek ozein, to smell, and ozone was named for its odour.
normal.cn: 前缀 oz- 来自希腊语「嗅」的动词，ozone 正是因气味得名。

normal.en: Ozone layer and ozone hole are the two phrases that keep the word in the news.
normal.cn: ozone layer 与 ozone hole 是让这个词不断出现在新闻里的两个搭配。

normal.en: An -e ending and an -ic suffix give ozonic and ozonise.
normal.cn: 词尾加 -e、加 -ic 等后缀就构成 ozonic 与 ozonise。

normal.en: Ozone is made of oxygen, carried a step further: three atoms instead of two.
normal.cn: ozone 由 oxygen 再进一步：三个原子取代两个。

normal.en: The word first meant the gas itself, and only later the layer it forms high up.
normal.cn: 这个词先说气体本身，后来才指它在高空形成的那一层。

abstract.en: Picture a thin blue veil floating high above the earth, catching the sun.
abstract.cn: 想象一层薄薄的蓝纱飘在地球上方，接住阳光。

abstract.en: Imagine the air tasting clean and electric right after a thunderstorm.
abstract.cn: 想象雷雨刚过时空气那种清洁又带电的味道。

abstract.en: See a shield ring around the planet with a small hole worn in it.
abstract.cn: 想象行星外圈一道护盾，上面被磨出了一个小洞。

examples.en: The ozone layer is slowly repairing itself.
examples.cn: 臭氧层正在缓慢自我修复。

examples.en: Her aunt is studying how ground-level ozone harms crops.
examples.cn: 她的阿姨正在研究近地面臭氧如何危害农作物。

examples.en: After the rain, the garden smelled of ozone and wet leaves.
examples.cn: 雨后，花园里有一股清新的空气和湿叶子味。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「欧宗」——欧洲老家头顶撑着一顶大罩，那是臭氧层替我们挡太阳；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 希腊语 ozein（嗅、散发气味）→ 德语 ozon（按气味命名）→ 法语 ozone → 英语 ozone；核心义「刺鼻的空气」→「高空盾层」。

sensesIntro.en: Ozone starts with the sharp-smelling gas, grows into the high layer and the fresh air, and then splits into its pollutant and cleaning uses.
sensesIntro.cn: ozone 从刺鼻的气体出发，长出高空层与清新空气的意义，再分出作为污染物与清洁剂的用法。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a thin pale blue shield floating high above the earth.
core.cn: 核心意象：地球上空悬浮的一层淡蓝色薄盾。

branches.en: The gas named for its smell is the base sense.
branches.cn: 因气味得名的气体是基础义项。

branches.en: The layer that the gas forms in the sky is the shield sense.
branches.cn: 气体在高空形成的那一层就是屏障义项。

branches.en: Fresh sea air and the feeling of something bracing grow out of the smell.
branches.cn: 清新海风与清爽振奋之感都从「气味」里长出来。

branches.en: Ozone near the ground turns the gas into a smog hazard.
branches.cn: 近地面的臭氧把这种气体变成烟雾危害。

branches.en: The odour itself and the gas as a cleaner are its working senses.
branches.cn: 气味本身与作为净化剂的臭氧是它的实用处义项。

intro.en: Ozone is formed with a Greek smell root and German and French endings, and modern English adds -ic, -ise, and -sphere.
intro.cn: ozone 由希腊语「嗅」词根与德法词尾构成，现代英语又加上 -ic、-ise、-sphere 等部分。

latinIntro.en: Ozone has no direct Latin ancestor; its scientific relatives are formed inside modern languages on the Greek root ozein.
latinIntro.cn: ozone 没有直接的拉丁语祖先；它的科学同族词都是在近代语言里用希腊词根 ozein 构成。

items.example: Ozein is the oldest piece of the word.
items.exampleCN: ozein 是这个词最古老的部分。

items.meaning: the gas with a sharp smell
items.example: The German chemist gave the gas this name.
items.exampleCN: 德国化学家给这种气体取了这个名字。

items.example: Ozone reaches English from French science.
items.exampleCN: ozone 是从法国科学作品进入英语的。

items.example: The suffix -ic makes ozonic.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ic 构成 ozonic。

items.example: The suffix -ous makes ozonous.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ous 构成 ozonous。

items.example: The suffix -ise makes ozonise.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ise 构成 ozonise。

items.example: The form -sphere combines with ozone to make ozonosphere.
items.exampleCN: 构词成分 -sphere 与 ozone 合成 ozonosphere。

items.meaning: the gas ozone is made from
items.example: Ozone is a rare form of oxygen.
items.exampleCN: 臭氧是氧的一种少见形态。

definition_zh: 协定；公约；条约；盟约
definition_en: a formal agreement between people, groups, or countries to do something or to keep peace
core_image: 两只手紧紧握住，掌心之间压着一纸约定
scene: 两国代表在桌前交换文件，郑重承诺互不侵犯。The two envoys signed a pact promising not to attack each other.
sceneCN: 这里 pact 是「协定、条约」（第 1 个义项：团体或国家之间的正式约定）；句意：两国代表在桌前交换文件，郑重承诺互不侵犯。

pos.zh: 协定；公约；条约；盟约

derivatives.zh: 约定；契约，由词根加名词后缀 -ion 构成，较书面
契约的；由约定产生的
撞击；影响，与 pact 同源于拉丁 pangere，只是前缀不同
协议；契约，形容约定的紧凑与牢靠

senses.title: A promise fixed between two sides
senses.definition: a formal, solemn agreement between two people or groups
senses.definitionCN: 两人或两方之间正式的郑重约定
senses.example: The two friends made a pact to run every morning.
senses.exampleCN: 两个朋友约定每天早上跑步。
senses.why: The Latin verb for fastening gives the word its picture: a promise nailed down so that both sides are bound.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语中「固定」的动词给出画面：把承诺钉牢，让双方都被拴住，这就是约定。

senses.title: A peace agreement between countries
senses.definition: a treaty in which nations agree to stop fighting or support each other
senses.definitionCN: 国家间同意停止交战或相互支援的条约
senses.example: The two countries signed a peace pact last year.
senses.exampleCN: 两国去年签署了和平条约。
senses.why: A fastened promise on a national scale becomes a signed treaty that ends or prevents war.
senses.whyCN: 把「钉牢的承诺」放大到国家层面，就成了一纸结束或防止战争的签约条约。

senses.title: A secret or personal vow
senses.definition: a private pledge, sometimes hidden, between close people
senses.definitionCN: 亲密之人之间有时不公开的誓言
senses.example: They kept their pact a secret from the rest of the family.
senses.exampleCN: 他们把这个约定对家里其他人保密。
senses.why: Because the agreement binds only its makers, it can also be a quiet vow shared by a few.
senses.whyCN: 因为约定只约束缔约的人，它也就可以是少数人之间悄悄分享的誓言。

senses.title: A binding promise in general
senses.definition: any commitment that holds a person to a course of action
senses.definitionCN: 任何把人约束在某种做法上的承诺
senses.example: The company made a pact with itself to cut waste by half.
senses.exampleCN: 公司与自己立下约定：把浪费减半。
senses.why: The word means a promise fixed in place, so it easily widens to any binding pledge.
senses.whyCN: 这个词本义是把承诺固定住，所以很容易扩展到任何有约束力的保证。

senses.title: A deal between unlikely partners
senses.definition: a bargain between people or sides not normally allied
senses.definitionCN: 彼此本不结盟的人或方面之间的交易
senses.example: The rebels made a pact with the very army they once fought.
senses.exampleCN: 叛军与他们曾经交战的军队达成了契约。
senses.why: The words pact and peace treaty share the idea of enemies forced together and then bound.
senses.whyCN: pact 与「和平条约」共享一个想法：敌人被强行拉到一起，然后被绑住。

senses.title: A covenant of ancient or religious weight
senses.definition: a sacred or long-standing agreement with a heavy moral weight
senses.definitionCN: 带有沉重道德分量的神圣或古老约定
senses.example: Older books describe the covenant and the pact between man and earth.
senses.exampleCN: 较古老的书里记载了人与土地之间的圣约。
senses.why: The oldest usage gives the word a solemn tone, so it still suits vows of faith or kinship.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的用法赋予这个词庄重的语气，所以它至今适合用于信仰或亲缘的誓约。

senses.title: Pact as peace terms in documents
senses.definition: the set of conditions written down in a signed agreement
senses.definitionCN: 写进已签协议中的一套条件
senses.example: A clause in the pact allows either side to leave.
senses.exampleCN: 协定中的一项条款允许任何一方退出。
senses.why: Once a promise is fastened to paper, the paper itself takes the name and its clauses are called the pact.
senses.whyCN: 承诺一旦钉到纸上，纸本身就用了这个名字，其中的条款也被称作 pact。

senses.title: A pact among nations for working together
senses.definition: a treaty that joins countries in a shared policy or defence plan
senses.definitionCN: 把多国联合起来的共同政策或防务条约
senses.example: The group of allies signed a pact on trade and defence.
senses.exampleCN: 同盟各国签署了贸易与防务协定。
senses.why: With more parties the single promise becomes a wide alliance, so pact also means a joining treaty.
senses.whyCN: 缔约方一多，单个承诺就变成广泛的联盟，所以 pact 也指联合条约。

intro.en: Pact comes from the Latin pactus, a thing fastened or agreed, from the verb pangere, to fasten or fix.
intro.cn: pact 来自拉丁语 pactus（固定的、商定的），源于动词 pangere（钉牢、固定）。

items.en: The reconstructed root pag- means to fix or fasten, the sense behind the later verb.
items.cn: 重构词根 pag- 意为「固定、钉牢」，这是后来动词意义的来源。

items.en: Pangere means to fasten or drive in, and pactum is a thing agreed and fixed.
items.cn: pangere 意为「钉牢、钉入」，pactum 指议定并被定下的事项。

items.en: Pactum grows into pactus, used in law for what was bargained and settled.
items.cn: pactum 演变为 pactus，在拉丁法律文中指议价后定下的事情。

items.en: Pacte carries the word into the everyday speech of France.
items.cn: Pacte 把这个词带进法语的日常用语。

items.en: Pact appears in English first in legal records and then in ordinary prose.
items.cn: pact 先在英语的法律文书里出现，随后进入一般文章。

items.en: From the peace treaties of later centuries, pact becomes a general word for a treaty.
items.cn: 到近代的和平条约时期，pact 成为指条约的通用词。

note.en: Pact is a short word: it looks like other short words ending in act, and it shares its meaning ground with treaty, deal, and alliance.
note.cn: pact 是个短词：它和别的 act 结尾短词形近，意义上又与 treaty、deal、alliance 相邻。

entries.definition: a formal agreement
entries.definitionCN: 正式约定；契约

entries.definition: a formal agreement between parties
entries.definitionCN: 各方之间的正式协议；与 pact 同源于拉丁 pangere

entries.definition: a hit or a strong effect
entries.definitionCN: 撞击；强烈影响；与 pact 同源，前缀不同

entries.definition: a formal written agreement between countries
entries.definitionCN: 国家间的正式书面协定

entries.definition: an informal agreement or bargain
entries.definitionCN: 非正式的协议；交易

entries.definition: a union of groups who agree to work together
entries.definitionCN: 结盟；为合作而联合

normalIntro.en: Pact is the noun of a promise packed and sealed: the verb pangere means to fasten it down.
normalIntro.cn: pact 是把承诺打包封住的动名词：拉丁动词意为把它钉牢。

normal.en: Pact and pack share the p-a-c start, and a pact packs a promise into a fixed shape.
normal.cn: pact 与 pack 都以 pac 开头，而 pact 就是把承诺打包成固定的形状。

normal.en: The word came through French pacte from Latin pactus, a thing fastened.
normal.cn: 这个词经法语 pacte 来自拉丁语 pactus，意为「被固定之物」。

normal.en: Make a pact and break a pact are the two most common verb phrases.
normal.cn: make a pact 与 break a pact 是它最常见的两个动词搭配。

normal.en: Pact and impact share the Latin verb pangere, to drive in; one fastens a promise, the other drives a blow.
normal.cn: pact 与 impact 共享拉丁动词 pangere（钉入）：一个钉住承诺，一个打入一击。

normal.en: Compare treaty: a treaty is written between states, a pact can join people or nations.
normal.cn: 对比 treaty：treaty 多指国家间的书面文件，pact 既可指人也可指国家结约。

abstract.en: Picture two hands shaking hard, with paper pressed between the palms.
abstract.cn: 想象两只手用力相握，掌心之间压着一张纸。

abstract.en: Imagine a heavy nail driven through a promise on a desk.
abstract.cn: 想象一根粗钉子把桌上的承诺钉住。

abstract.en: See two old enemies standing at one table, each holding a copy.
abstract.cn: 想象一对宿敌站在同一张桌前，各持一份文件。

examples.en: The sisters made a pact never to lie to each other.
examples.cn: 姐妹俩约定彼此永远不说谎。

examples.en: The two nations signed a non-aggression pact in the spring.
examples.cn: 两国在春天签署了互不侵犯条约。

examples.en: Breaking the pact cost them the support of their allies.
examples.cn: 违反这份约定让他们失去了盟友的支持。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「拍克特」——签协议时两人用力一拍手，再拍一下纸，约定就成了；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 pangere（钉牢、固定）→ pactus（固定之物）→ 中世纪拉丁 pactus（议定事项）→ 古法语 pacte → 中古英语 pact；核心义「被钉牢的承诺」。

sensesIntro.en: Pact begins as a promise fixed between two sides, widens to national treaties and secret vows, and finally points to the paper and the alliance it creates.
sensesIntro.cn: pact 从双方钉牢的承诺出发，扩展到国家条约与私下誓约，最后指向那张文件以及它所结成的联盟。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two hands gripped over a sealed sheet of paper.
core.cn: 核心意象：两只手握在一起，掌下压着一张封好的纸。

branches.en: The fixed promise and any binding commitment are the core senses.
branches.cn: 钉牢的承诺与任何有约束力的保证是核心义项。

branches.en: When the two sides are nations, the pact becomes a treaty or alliance.
branches.cn: 当双方是国家时，约定就变成条约或同盟。

branches.en: Private vows and deals between odd partners keep the word close to its makers.
branches.cn: 私下誓约与奇特伙伴之间的交易让这个词仍贴近缔约人。

branches.en: An ancient or sacred agreement keeps the solemn tone of the oldest sense.
branches.cn: 古老或神圣的约定保留了最早义项的庄重语气。

branches.en: Once sealed on paper, the document and its clauses carry the name.
branches.cn: 一旦封到纸上，文件及其条款就沿用了这个名字。

intro.en: Pact is a bare Latin noun, and its family is formed from the root pag- or pact- with English endings.
intro.cn: pact 是裸露的拉丁名词，它的同族词由 pag- 或 pact- 词根加英语词尾构成。

latinIntro.en: Latin pangere means to fasten, and pactum is a thing agreed and fixed.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 pangere 意为「钉牢」，pactum 指议定并定下之事。

items.example: Pangere gives the fastening image of the word.
items.exampleCN: pangere 提供这个词「钉牢」的意象。

items.example: Pactum is the direct source.
items.exampleCN: pactum 是直接来源。

items.example: Pacte brings the word into French.
items.exampleCN: pacte 把这个词带入法语。

items.example: Pact keeps the settled noun sense.
items.exampleCN: pact 保留了「议定」的名词含义。

items.example: The suffix -ion makes paction.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ion 构成 paction。

items.example: The suffix -al makes pactional.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -al 构成 pactional。

items.example: The suffix -s makes pacts.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -s 构成 pacts。

items.example: The prefix com- with pact gives compact, an agreement held together.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 com- 与 pact 合成 compact，指把各方捆在一起的协议。

items.example: The prefix im- with pact gives impact, a blow driven in.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 im- 与 pact 合成 impact，指打进的一击。

definition_zh: 塔；宝塔；（佛教寺院的）佛塔
definition_en: a tall religious tower with several decorated roofs, built in East Asia, usually for Buddhist relics or temples
core_image: 一座层层叠起、檐角上翘的多层宝塔，塔顶一只尖铃直指天空
scene: 雨后的山寺里，一座多层宝塔静静立在古松之间，檐角的风铃轻轻作响。A layer of cloud drifted past the top of the pagoda before the sunrise.
sceneCN: 这里 pagoda 是「塔、宝塔」（第 1 个义项：东方佛教寺院中层层叠顶的多层塔）；句意：日出之前，一层云雾从塔顶飘过。

pos.zh: 塔；宝塔；（佛教寺院的）佛塔

derivatives.zh: 词根加过去分词构成形容词，义为「宝塔形的」
规则复数形式，指多座宝塔

senses.title: A many-tiered tower of East Asia
senses.definition: a tall tower with several projecting roofs, built in China, Japan, and other parts of East Asia for religious use
senses.definitionCN: 在中国、日本及东亚其他地区建造的、带有一层层突出屋檐的高塔，用于宗教用途
senses.example: Pilgrims climbed the stone steps beside the pagoda.
senses.exampleCN: 朝圣者们沿着宝塔旁的石头台阶往上走。
senses.why: The word came to English through the Portuguese travellers who first described these towers, so the image of a tiered tower sits at its core.
senses.whyCN: 这个词经由最先描述此类塔的葡萄牙航海者进入英语，所以「层层叠起的塔」正是它的核心形象。

senses.title: A Buddhist reliquary tower
senses.definition: a Buddhist structure that houses sacred relics or sutras and stands at the heart of a temple
senses.definitionCN: 存放圣物或经卷、位于寺院核心地带的佛教建筑
senses.example: A small gold case of relics was kept inside the pagoda.
senses.exampleCN: 舍利被装在一个小金匣里，安放在佛塔内。
senses.why: The pyramid-shaped round tower of ancient India developed into the East Asian tiered tower, and its main duty was to guard sacred remains.
senses.whyCN: 古印度那种尖锥状的圆塔演变为东亚的层叠塔，最核心的职责就是守护圣物。

senses.title: A tiered tower in general
senses.definition: any tall building with a series of stacked roofs or tiers, even when not a religious one
senses.definitionCN: 泛指任何带有一层层屋顶或层级的塔式高建筑，不一定用于宗教
senses.example: The old library has a pagoda in its courtyard.
senses.exampleCN: 那座老图书馆的庭院里有一座塔式建筑。
senses.why: Once the word was known in English, the stacked-roof shape itself could be borrowed for buildings that are not Buddhist at all.
senses.whyCN: 这个词进入英语后，「层叠屋顶」这个外形被借用来指并非佛教用途的建筑物。

senses.title: A pagoda-shaped ornament or object
senses.titleCN: 宝塔形的物件；塔形装饰
senses.definition: a small object, ornament, or piece of roof that is shaped like a tiered tower
senses.definitionCN: 形状像层叠高塔的小物件、装饰品或屋顶部件
senses.example: She kept a jade pagoda on the shelf beside her desk.
senses.exampleCN: 她在书桌旁的架子上放着一座玉制宝塔。
senses.why: The distinctive silhouette became a familiar decoration, so the name travelled from the building to the shaped object.
senses.whyCN: 塔的轮廓极为醒目，成了常见的装饰母题，于是名称也从建筑转移到了造型之物上。

senses.title: A pagoda-shaped mountain peak
senses.definition: a steep mountain peak whose narrow summit makes it look like a tower
senses.definitionCN: 山顶收窄、看起来像一座塔的陡峭山峰
senses.example: Two hikers roped up to reach the pagoda that crowns the range.
senses.exampleCN: 两名登山者系上绳索，去攀登那道山脊顶上形如宝塔的峰尖。
senses.why: In travel writing the word often names natural rock that copies the tower outline, extending the shape from architecture to landscape.
senses.whyCN: 在游记中，这个词常用来指模仿塔形的天然岩石，把同一造型从建筑延伸到山水。

senses.title: A temple or shrine complex
senses.definition: used loosely in older travel writing for a whole temple site with a tower at its centre
senses.definitionCN: 旧时游记中较宽泛的用法，指以塔为中心的整个寺院建筑群
senses.example: The old journal describes a pagoda of white stone with a hundred shaded courtyards.
senses.exampleCN: 那本旧游记描写了一座由白色石材建成、拥有一百个阴凉庭院的塔院。
senses.why: Early European visitors saw the tower and the whole precinct together, so the single word could stand for the shrine site itself.
senses.whyCN: 早期欧洲访客把塔与整个建筑群看成一体，于是一个词就能代表整座塔院。

intro.en: Pagoda reached English through Portuguese, which borrowed it from South Asian languages first, and its ultimate origin is still debated.
intro.cn: pagoda 经葡萄牙语进入英语，而葡萄牙语又是从南亚语言借来的，其最终来源至今仍有争议。

items.en: A reconstructed form such as dhatu-garbha, meaning relic chamber, is often suggested for the relic shrine idea.
items.cn: 一般认为，塔形佛塔的「舍利室」概念可追溯到重构形式 dhatu-garbha 一类词语（重构形式，存疑）。

items.en: Some scholars link the word to Prakrit bhagodio or Tamil form pakavati, but no link is certain.
items.cn: 有学者把该词与俗语 bhagodio 或泰米尔语 pakavati 联系起来，但均无定论。

items.en: Portuguese traders in the East recorded pagode for the tiered towers and temple images they saw.
items.cn: 十六世纪的葡萄牙商人在东方用 pagode 记录他们所见的层叠塔和寺中神像。

items.en: English travellers brought the word home, and it shifted its meaning towards the tower itself.
items.cn: 英国旅行者把这个词带回国内，其含义逐渐聚焦到塔本身。

items.en: Writers such as those describing Eastern travel fixed the spelling pagoda for the many-tiered tower.
items.cn: 描写东方见闻的作家固定了 pagoda 的拼写，用它专指多层宝塔。

note.en: Pagoda is a tower of East Asian faith and travel writing, close to temple, shrine, and other tower words.
note.cn: pagoda 是东亚宗教与游记中的塔，与 temple、shrine 以及其他「塔」类词相邻。

entries.definition: the older Portuguese form of the word
entries.definitionCN: 葡萄牙语中的早期形式，与英语词同源，只是拼写相近

entries.definition: formed like a tiered tower
entries.definitionCN: 宝塔形的；拼写相近，构成相同词根

entries.definition: an older English spelling of the same word
entries.definitionCN: 同一词的旧式英语拼写

entries.definition: a religious building or the ground around it
entries.definitionCN: 寺庙；神殿；寺院

entries.definition: a dome-shaped Buddhist monument for relics
entries.definitionCN: 佛塔；窣堵坡（存放舍利的圆丘形佛塔）

entries.definition: a tall pointed church tower
entries.definitionCN: 教堂尖塔；尖顶

normalIntro.en: Pagoda is a tiered tower of East Asia, learned from Portuguese travellers of the sixteenth century.
normalIntro.cn: pagoda 是东亚的层叠宝塔，源自十六世纪葡萄牙旅行者的记录。

normal.en: The word entered English through Portuguese pagode, from languages of the East.
normal.cn: 这个词经葡萄牙语 pagode 从东方语言进入英语。

normal.en: A pagoda rises in tiers, each roof a little smaller than the one below.
normal.cn: 宝塔一层层向上收拢，每层屋檐都比下面一层略小。

normal.en: Pagoda and temple often appear together: a temple pagoda.
normal.cn: pagoda 常与 temple 连用：temple pagoda 即寺塔。

normal.en: The plural is pagodas, simply adding an s.
normal.cn: 复数就是 pagodas，直接加 s。

normal.en: Repetition in speech and eye and mind helps foreign words stick.
normal.cn: 把拼写、发音和含义放在一起反复对照，外来词才记得住。

abstract.en: Picture a stack of roofs, each one smaller, crowned by a bell.
abstract.cn: 想象一摞屋顶层层变小，最上面挂着一只铃。

abstract.en: Imagine a stone box of holy relics under the lowest tier.
abstract.cn: 想象最底层下面藏着一个装着圣物的石匣。

abstract.en: See the same outline in a museum shelf ornament or a lonely peak.
abstract.cn: 在博物的架上小摆件或一座孤峰里看见同样的轮廓。

examples.en: The pagoda is said to have been built over a thousand years ago.
examples.cn: 据说这座宝塔建于一千多年前。

examples.en: Two old pagodas stand at the edge of the lake.
examples.cn: 湖边立着两座古老的宝塔。

examples.en: From the hill you can see the pointed roofs of the pagoda above the trees.
examples.cn: 从山上望去，能看见树梢上方宝塔的层层尖顶。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「爬上塔」——pagoda 读起来像「爬过塔」，层层往上爬；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 经葡萄牙语 pagode 借入，来源于南亚的俗语或泰米尔语形式（一般认为与 dhatu-garbha 一类「舍利室」词语有关，但最终词源存疑，不作定论），核心意象「层层叠起的塔」。

sensesIntro.en: Pagoda first means a tiered Buddhist tower, then its relic function, and from there the shape spreads to buildings, ornaments, and even peaks.
sensesIntro.cn: pagoda 先指层层叠顶的佛塔，再指它存放舍利的用途；由此这一外形又扩展到塔式建筑、塔形器物，乃至山峰。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a many-tiered tower, each roof smaller than the last, ending in a bell.
core.cn: 核心意象：层层收拢的多层塔，每层屋顶都比下一层小，塔顶挂铃。

branches.en: The everyday sense is the tall tiered tower.
branches.cn: 日常义项就是那座层层叠起的高塔。

branches.en: Its religious duty is to guard holy remains.
branches.cn: 佛塔的宗教职责是守护圣物。

branches.en: Any tiered tower may be called by the name, religious or not.
branches.cn: 无论是否用于宗教，任何层叠塔式建筑都可这样称呼。

branches.en: The shape travels from buildings to small ornaments.
branches.cn: 这一造型从建筑迁移到小型装饰物。

branches.en: Travel writing uses the word for a temple site and for peak shapes.
branches.cn: 游记中既用指整座塔院，也用来形容山峰。

intro.en: Pagoda has no English affixes; its parts are the Portuguese loan form and the travel-writing compounds built on it.
intro.cn: pagoda 没有可拆的英语词缀，可拆的部分是葡萄牙语借形，以及旅行文学中围绕它构成的复合词。

latinIntro.en: Pagoda has no Latin root; it is a loanword from the East through Portuguese.
latinIntro.cn: pagoda 没有拉丁词根，是经葡萄牙语转借的东方外来词。

items.example: Portuguese pagode is the direct source of the English word.
items.exampleCN: 葡萄牙语 pagode 是英语词的直接来源。

items.meaning: the final vowel added in the English form
items.meaningCN: 英语形式末尾添加的 a
items.example: The English form finishes with -a where Portuguese has -e.
items.exampleCN: 英语形式以 -a 结尾，而葡萄牙语用 -e。

items.example: Pagod was a common spelling in older travel books.
items.exampleCN: 在较早的游记里 pagod 是一种常见的拼写。

items.meaning: a pagoda belonging to a temple
items.example: Temple pagoda names the tower that belongs to a monastery.
items.exampleCN: temple pagoda 指属于寺院的塔。

items.example: Relics were kept in the lowest tier of the tower.
items.exampleCN: 圣物存放在塔的最底层。

items.meaning: a tree with tiered flower clusters
items.meaningCN: 槐树一类开层状花序的树
items.example: The pagoda tree is named for its flower shape.
items.exampleCN: 这种树因花序的形状而得名。

items.example: A three-storey tower is a small tower.
items.exampleCN: 三层塔就是一座很小的塔。

items.example: The shrine and the tower stood together.
items.exampleCN: 神殿与塔并立在一起。

definition_zh: 艰苦细致的；煞费苦心的；一丝不苟的（做法的）；细致认真的（人）
definition_en: done with great care and effort, paying attention to every small detail
core_image: 一个人伏在案前，把每一处细小的地方都反复核对到深夜
scene: 天已经亮了，桌上的台灯才被关掉，那位抄写员一整夜都在逐字校对古籍。The painstaking work of the copyist saved three centuries of records from being lost.
sceneCN: 这里 painstaking 是「艰苦细致的」（第 1 个义项：做事付出极大耐心、认真对待每一处细节）；句意：这位抄写员艰苦细致的工作让三个世纪的文件免于散失。

pos.zh: 艰苦细致的；煞费苦心的

derivatives.zh: 形容词加 -ly 构成副词，义为「煞费苦心地；一丝不苟地」
形容词加 -ness 构成名词，义为「一丝不苟；认真细致」
pain 的复数，本词即取其「辛劳、费心」之义，常用短语 take pains to do

senses.title: Showing great care and effort in work
senses.titleCN: 艰苦细致的；煞费苦心的
senses.definition: acting with great care and hard work, and paying close attention to every small part
senses.definitionCN: 做事时付出极大心力，密切关注每一个细小部分
senses.example: It took painstaking work to check every page of the register.
senses.exampleCN: 核对登记册的每一页是件艰苦细致的工作。
senses.why: The word began as a phrase for someone who takes pains, meaning who goes to great trouble, so effort and care are built into it.
senses.whyCN: 这个词最初是「takes pains」的合成说法，pains 在此义为「辛劳、费心」，所以「付出心力」与「细致」是它自带的含义。

senses.title: Thorough and detailed in method
senses.titleCN: 细致透彻的；一丝不苟的（方法）
senses.definition: referring to a method or process carried out slowly, fully, and without skipping steps
senses.definitionCN: 指某种方法或过程进行得缓慢、完整，不跳过任何步骤
senses.example: The painters used a painstaking process of thin, repeated coats.
senses.exampleCN: 画工们采用的是一层薄涂层反复涂抹的细致工序。
senses.why: When the word is used of a process rather than a person, the effort turns into many small careful stages.
senses.whyCN: 当它形容的是过程而不是人时，那份心力就体现为许多细小而谨慎的步骤。

senses.title: Careful and meticulous in character
senses.titleCN: 一丝不苟的；做事极认真的（人）
senses.definition: describing a person who is extremely careful and hardworking by habit
senses.definitionCN: 形容一个人习惯上极为认真、肯下苦功
senses.example: A painstaking editor read the draft three times before it went to press.
senses.exampleCN: 一位一丝不苟的编辑在付印前把稿子读了三遍。
senses.why: The habit sense transfers the action to the person, so a painstaking teacher or clerk is simply someone who always goes to this trouble.
senses.whyCN: 这一习惯义把动作转给了人：一位 painstaking 的老师或职员，就是把这种费心当成习惯的人。

senses.title: Slow and laboured in pace
senses.titleCN: 缓慢费力的；进度艰难的
senses.definition: done slowly and with noticeable effort, often suggesting that progress is hard won
senses.definitionCN: 进行得缓慢且明显费力，常暗示进展来之不易
senses.example: Progress was painstaking, one village at a time.
senses.exampleCN: 进展十分艰难，一个村子一个村子地慢慢推进。
senses.why: Because pain sits inside the word, it can also describe pace, where the effort itself is the point and speed is the cost.
senses.whyCN: 因为 pain 这层「费神」的意思藏在词里，它也能描述速度：付出的努力本身就是代价，所以显得慢。

senses.title: Producing a record taken great pains over
senses.titleCN: 经艰苦细致做出的（成果）
senses.definition: used of a result, such as a map or archive, that clearly shows long and careful work
senses.definitionCN: 用于描述地图、档案等成果，显示其背后付出了长久而细致的工夫
senses.example: The painstaking map shows every field boundary from two hundred years ago.
senses.exampleCN: 这幅精心绘制的地图标出了两百年前每一道田界。
senses.why: The same idea reaches the object: a thing that embodies long effort is itself called painstaking.
senses.whyCN: 同样的意思也落到成品上：凝聚了长久心血的物件本身就被称作 painstaking。

intro.en: Painstaking is a compound built in English from pains, in its older sense of effort or trouble, and the verb take.
intro.cn: painstaking 是英语内部构成的复合词，来自 pains（旧义为「辛劳、费心」）与动词 take。

items.en: Latin poena means a penalty, a price paid, or pain.
items.cn: 拉丁语 poena 意为惩罚、代价或痛苦。

items.en: Old French peine means pain, trouble, or effort.
items.cn: 古法语 peine 意为痛苦、麻烦或辛劳。

items.en: English pain takes on the sense of effort, as in take pains to do something.
items.cn: 中古英语 pain 发展出「费力」之义，形成 take pains to do something 的用法。

items.en: The phrase taking pains is joined into the adjective pains-taking.
items.cn: 十六世纪，taking pains 这一短语被合成形容词 pains-taking。

items.en: The spelling settles as painstaking and comes to mean careful and diligent.
items.cn: 十七世纪拼写固定为 painstaking，意为认真勤勉。

note.en: Painstaking is one member of a family of careful words, close to painstakingly, meticulous, and diligent.
note.cn: painstaking 属于「认真」类词族，与 painstakingly、meticulous、diligent 相邻。

entries.definition: in a very careful way
entries.definitionCN: 煞费苦心地；一丝不苟地

entries.definition: the quality of being very careful
entries.definitionCN: 一丝不苟的品质

entries.definition: effort or trouble in take pains
entries.definitionCN: （在 take pains 中）辛劳、费心

entries.definition: showing great attention to detail
entries.definitionCN: 一丝不苟的；极细心的

entries.definition: working hard with steady care
entries.definitionCN: 勤勉的；用功的

entries.definition: complete, with nothing left out
entries.definitionCN: 彻底的；周密的

normalIntro.en: Painstaking joins pains, meaning effort, to taking, so it means taking trouble over the work.
normalIntro.cn: painstaking 把义为「辛劳」的 pains 与 taking 结合起来，意思是肯为工作费心出力。

normal.en: Think of the phrase take pains to do something, which means to take great trouble.
normal.cn: 回想短语 take pains to do something，意思是出大力气、下苦功。

normal.en: Here pain is not bodily hurt but effort, as in the plural pains.
normal.cn: 这里的 pain 并非身体的疼痛，而是「费心」，取 pains 复数之义。

normal.en: The adverb painstakingly simply adds -ly to the same word.
normal.cn: 副词 painstakingly 就是这个形容词加 -ly。

normal.en: It often goes with work, research, and attention to detail.
normal.cn: 它常与 work、research、attention to detail 这样的搭配同现。

normal.en: Compare painstaking with painful: one is about effort, the other about hurt.
normal.cn: 对比 painstaking 与 painful：前者说的是费力，后者说的是疼痛。

abstract.en: Picture a lamp still lit while the rest of the house is dark.
abstract.cn: 想象整座房子都黑了，只有一盏灯还亮着。

abstract.en: Imagine checking a long list twice, tick by tick.
abstract.cn: 想象把一张长长的清单逐项核对两遍。

abstract.en: See a clerk who stays late by habit, not by order.
abstract.cn: 想象一位职员不是因为被要求，而是出于习惯才留下来加班。

examples.en: Rebuilding the broken window frame took painstaking care.
examples.cn: 修复破损的窗框需要极其细致的心思。

examples.en: Her painstaking notes later became the basis of the whole report.
examples.cn: 她一丝不苟的笔记后来成了整份报告的基础。

examples.en: The team carried out a slow and painstaking check of every sample.
examples.cn: 团队对每一个样本都做了缓慢而细致的核查。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「陪史太认真」——一位老抄写员把史书逐字陪读、逐字校勘，认真到每个标点都不放过；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 poena（惩罚、代价）→ 古法语 peine（痛苦、辛劳）→ 中古英语 pains（辛劳、费心）→ 合成 pains + taking → painstaking「肯下苦功、细致入微」，核心义「为细致付出心力」。

sensesIntro.en: Painstaking first describes careful, effortful work, then a thorough method, a careful person, a slow pace, and finally a result that shows all that effort.
sensesIntro.cn: painstaking 先形容艰苦细致的工作，再指细致透彻的方法、认真的人、缓慢费力的进程，最后指凝聚这些心血的成果。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a lit lamp over a desk, with every line checked again.
core.cn: 核心意象：案头一盏灯，每一行文字都被再核对一遍。

branches.en: Careful effortful work is the central sense.
branches.cn: 艰苦细致的工作是核心义项。

branches.en: Applied to a process, the care becomes many small steps.
branches.cn: 用于过程时，这份认真体现为许多细小步骤。

branches.en: Applied to a person, it becomes a settled habit.
branches.cn: 用于人时，它成为一种固定的习惯。

branches.en: The effort also shows in a slow, hard-won pace.
branches.cn: 这份心力也体现在缓慢、来之不易的进度上。

branches.en: Work done with pains leaves a record that speaks for itself.
branches.cn: 下过苦功的劳动会留下自己说话的成果。

intro.en: Painstaking is a compound of pains and taking, with -ly and -ness forming its close family.
intro.cn: painstaking 由 pains 与 taking 复合而成，-ly 与 -ness 构成它的同族词。

latinIntro.en: The pain part goes back through Old French peine to Latin poena, meaning penalty.
latinIntro.cn: 其中的 pain 经古法语 peine 追溯至拉丁语 poena，意为「惩罚」。

items.example: Latin poena already carries the idea of a price paid.
items.exampleCN: 拉丁语 poena 已含「付出代价」之意。

items.example: Old French peine brings the word into English.
items.exampleCN: 古法语 peine 把该词带入英语。

items.example: Pains in the plural means effort, as in take pains.
items.exampleCN: 复数的 pains 表「辛劳」，如 take pains 中。

items.example: Taking is the verb part of the compound.
items.exampleCN: taking 是这个复合词的动词部分。

items.example: Painstaking joins the effort to the doing of it.
items.exampleCN: painstaking 把心力与行动合成一个形容词。

items.example: The suffix -ly forms painstakingly.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ly 构成 painstakingly。

items.example: The suffix -ness forms painstakingness.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ness 构成 painstakingness。

items.example: Pain in modern use usually means bodily hurt.
items.exampleCN: 现代用法中 pain 多指身体上的疼痛。

items.example: Painful keeps the hurt sense, unlike painstaking.
items.exampleCN: painful 保留了「痛」的含义，与 painstaking 不同。

definition_zh: 古人类学家；研究早期人类化石与人类起源的专家
definition_en: a scientist who studies the fossils and remains of early humans and their ancestors
core_image: 一位戴着手套的学者，在探方里用刷子小心刷开化石周围的泥土
scene: 山谷里的发掘现场已经挖到两米深，土层中露出一块头骨，队里的学者不敢用铁锹，改用小刷子一点点清理。A paleoanthropologist carefully brushed the soil from the skull.
sceneCN: 这里 paleoanthropologist 是「古人类学家」（第 1 个义项：以研究早期人类化石为主的科学家）；句意：一位古人类学家小心地刷去头骨上的泥土。

pos.zh: 古人类学家；研究早期人类化石的专家

collocations.zh: 一位顶尖的古人类学家
古人类学家兼化石搜寻者
古人类学家的野外考察

derivatives.zh: 去掉表人的后缀 -ist，义为「古人类学」这一学科
词干加形容词后缀 -ical，义为「古人类学的」
由 anthropo- 与 -logist 构成的基础词，义为「人类学家」，本词加上 paleo- 后专指研究古人类者

senses.title: A scientist who studies early human fossils
senses.titleCN: 古人类学家；人类起源研究者
senses.definition: a researcher who examines the bones, teeth, and other remains of early humans and their ancestors to understand how our species evolved
senses.definitionCN: 通过研究早期人类及其祖先的骨骼、牙齿和其他遗物，来理解人类如何演化的研究者
senses.example: The paleoanthropologist spent a month cleaning the jaw fragment in the lab.
senses.exampleCN: 这位古人类学家花了一个月时间在实验室里清理那块下颌骨碎片。
senses.why: The Greek base anthropos means human, paleo- means old, and -logist means a person who studies, so the person who studies old humans is named by the parts of the word itself.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语词根 anthropos 意为「人」，paleo- 意为「古老」，-logist 意为「研究某学科的人」，所以这个词的三个部分直接拼出「研究古人类的人」。

senses.title: A field researcher at a dig site
senses.titleCN: 野外发掘出身的古人类学家
senses.definition: specifically one who works on site, excavating and recording fossils in the field
senses.definitionCN: 特指在现场工作、在野外发掘并记录化石的古人类学家
senses.example: The paleoanthropologist mapped every stone in the trench before lifting the bones.
senses.exampleCN: 在取出骨骼之前，这位古人类学家先把探方里每一块石头都测绘定位。
senses.why: Because the job is built on finds made in the ground, the word often points to the person with a trowel rather than only to a theorist.
senses.whyCN: 因为这门学问建立在从地下挖出的发现之上，所以这个词常指拿着小铲的一线工作者，而不只是理论家。

senses.title: An interpreter of the fossil record
senses.definition: one who reads the evidence of fossils and places it in a theory of human evolution
senses.definitionCN: 解读化石证据，并把它们放进人类演化理论中的学者
senses.example: A paleoanthropologist argued that the pelvis showed upright walking.
senses.exampleCN: 一位古人类学家论证说，那个骨盆说明当时已能直立行走。
senses.why: Excavation alone is not enough, so the same word also names the scholar who turns bone shapes into claims about behaviour.
senses.whyCN: 仅有发掘还不够，所以这个词也指把骨骼形状转化为对行为之判断的学者。

senses.title: A professional based in a museum or university
senses.titleCN: 在博物馆或大学任职的古人类学家
senses.definition: a specialist who holds a post in a museum, university, or research institute rather than working only in the field
senses.definitionCN: 在博物馆、大学或研究机构任职、并不只做野外工作的专家
senses.example: As a paleoanthropologist at the museum, she cares for two hundred hominin teeth.
senses.exampleCN: 作为博物馆的古人类学家，她负责照管两百颗人科牙齿标本。
senses.why: The profession has an institutional life as well, so the word also labels a post, a collection, and a laboratory.
senses.whyCN: 这个职业也有其机构生活，因此这个词同样可以指一个职位、一批馆藏和一间实验室。

intro.en: Paleoanthropologist is a scientific compound of Greek parts: paleo, anthropos, and logist, built in modern times.
intro.cn: paleoanthropologist 是用希腊语成分拼成的现代科学复合词：paleo、anthropos 与 logist。

items.en: Greek palaios means old, and anthropos means a human being.
items.cn: 古希腊语 palaios 意为「古老的」，anthropos 意为「人」。

items.en: Scholars of the eighteenth and nineteenth centuries used such Greek forms to name new sciences.
items.cn: 十八、十九世纪的学者常用这类希腊语形式为新学科命名。

items.en: Anthropology, the study of human beings, is joined with paleo- to name the study of ancient humans.
items.cn: 研究人类的 anthropology 与 paleo- 结合，用来指对远古人类的研究。

items.en: Paleoanthropology is established as a field, and paleoanthropologist names its researcher.
items.cn: 二十世纪古人类学确立为一门学科，paleoanthropologist 用来指该领域的研究者。

items.en: American spelling uses paleo-, while British spelling also uses palaeo-.
items.cn: 美式拼写用 paleo-，英式还常见 palaeo- 的写法。

note.en: Paleoanthropologist sits at the meeting point of old, human, and study, near paleontology, archaeology, and anthropologist.
note.cn: paleoanthropologist 处在「古老、人类、研究」三者的交汇处，与 paleontology、archaeology、anthropologist 相邻。

entries.definition: the study of early humans and their ancestors
entries.definitionCN: 古人类学

entries.definition: a specialist in the study of human beings
entries.definitionCN: 人类学家

entries.definition: the British spelling of the same word
entries.definitionCN: 同一词的英式拼写

entries.definition: a specialist who studies past cultures through objects
entries.definitionCN: 考古学家

entries.definition: a specialist who studies fossils of ancient life
entries.definitionCN: 古生物学家

entries.definition: a specialist who studies monkeys and apes
entries.definitionCN: 灵长类动物学家

normalIntro.en: Paleoanthropologist is a clear three-part build: old, human, and one who studies.
normalIntro.cn: paleoanthropologist 由三个清楚的部分拼成：古老、人类、研究某学科的人。

normal.en: paleo- means old, as in paleontology, the study of ancient life.
normal.cn: paleo- 意为「古老」，如 paleontology（古生物学）中。

normal.en: anthropos is Greek for human, and anthropologist means a student of humanity.
normal.cn: anthropos 是希腊语「人」，anthropologist 即人类学家。

normal.en: -logist marks the person, while -logy marks the subject.
normal.cn: 后缀 -logist 指人，-logy 指学科。

normal.en: The plural is paleoanthropologists, and the British spelling uses palaeo-.
normal.cn: 复数是 paleoanthropologists，英式拼写用 palaeo-。

normal.en: Keep the separate vowel after paleo, so the word has an extra a before anthropo.
normal.cn: paleo 与 anthropo 之间保留了一个 a，读的时候不要吞掉。

abstract.en: Picture a brush and a torch, not a pick and a hammer.
abstract.cn: 想象一把刷子和一支手电，而不是镐和锤。

abstract.en: Imagine a trowel cutting clean soil, then cords marking every stone.
abstract.cn: 想象小铲一块块切出平整的土层，再用细绳给每块石头定位。

abstract.en: See a pelvis laid out under a lamp, with three scientists debating it.
abstract.cn: 想象一个骨盆标本摆在灯下，三位学者围着它争论。

examples.en: The paleoanthropologist explained why the new skull was so unusual.
examples.cn: 这位古人类学家解释了这颗新头骨为何如此特别。

examples.en: Two paleoanthropologists from the museum joined the dig in the autumn.
examples.cn: 博物馆的两位古人类学家在秋天加入了发掘。

examples.en: As a paleoanthropologist at the museum, she cares for older fossil teeth.
examples.cn: 作为博物馆的古人类学家，她负责照管年代久远的化石牙齿。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「怕累 + 安思罗 + 破落吉斯特」——怕累的学者却安于思考人类的过去，化石再破落也要一块块收拾；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 希腊语 palaios（古老的）+ anthropos（人）+ -logist（研究某学科的人）→ 现代科学复合词，意为「研究古人类的学者」；同族词还有 anthropology 与 paleontology。

sensesIntro.en: Paleoanthropologist first names the researcher of early human fossils, then the field excavator, the interpreter of evidence, and the museum post.
sensesIntro.cn: paleoanthropologist 先指研究早期人类化石的科学家，再指野外发掘者、证据解释者，以及在博物馆任职的职位。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a gloved hand brushing soil from a skull in a lit trench.
core.cn: 核心意象：戴着手套的手，在亮着灯的探方里刷去头骨上的泥土。

branches.en: The central sense is a scientist who studies early human remains.
branches.cn: 核心义项是研究早期人类遗骸的科学家。

branches.en: The same word covers the dig worker in the field.
branches.cn: 这个词同样覆盖在野外作业的发掘者。

branches.en: It also covers the interpreter who turns bones into a theory.
branches.cn: 它也指把骨骼转为理论的解释者。

branches.en: And it names a museum or university post.
branches.cn: 它还指博物馆或大学的职位。

branches.en: All the senses join at the question of how humans began.
branches.cn: 各义项都交汇在「人类从何而来」这个问题上。

intro.en: Paleoanthropologist is built from three Greek elements: paleo-, anthrop-, and -logist.
intro.cn: paleoanthropologist 由三个希腊语要素构成：paleo-、anthrop- 与 -logist。

latinIntro.en: The word itself is Greek in origin; Latin and other European languages only passed the forms on to English.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词本身源自希腊语，拉丁语和其他欧洲语言只是把相关形式转渡给英语。

items.example: Paleo- appears in paleontology as well.
items.exampleCN: paleo- 也见于 paleontology 中。

items.example: Anthrop- appears in anthropology and philanthropy.
items.exampleCN: anthrop- 出现在 anthropology 与 philanthropy 中。

items.example: The suffix -logy names a field of study.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -logy 表示一门学科。

items.example: The suffix -logist names the researcher.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -logist 指研究者。

items.example: -ist keeps the sense of a person who practises a subject.
items.exampleCN: -ist 表示从事某门学问的人。

items.example: The suffix -ical forms the adjective paleoanthropological.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ical 构成形容词 paleoanthropological。

items.example: British spelling writes palaeo- with an extra a.
items.exampleCN: 英式拼写作 palaeo-，多一个 a。

items.example: Paleoanthropology is the field, the person is its worker.
items.exampleCN: paleoanthropology 是学科，paleoanthropologist 是从事者。

items.meaning: a member of the human branch
items.example: Hominin fossils are the main evidence studied.
items.exampleCN: 人科化石是所研究的主要证据。

items.meaning: a member of the great ape family
items.example: Hominid covers a wider family than hominin.
items.exampleCN: hominid 的家族范围比 hominin 更宽。

definition_zh: 娇惯；溺爱；纵容；精心呵护，使舒适
definition_en: to treat someone with too much kindness and attention, or to look after someone so well that they are extremely comfortable
core_image: 细心喂饭的人：把最好的食物一口一口送到嘴边
scene: 周末的清晨，一家人围着婴儿床忙前忙后，喂奶、换衣、轻轻哼歌。The whole family pampered the new baby over the weekend.
sceneCN: 这里 pamper 是「娇惯、精心呵护」（第 1 个义项：对某人过分体贴）；句意：整个周末，全家人都在精心呵护这个新生儿。

pos.zh: 娇惯；溺爱；纵容
精心呵护；使舒适享受

collocations.zh: 好好犒劳自己；享受一下

collocations.phrase: be pampered from head to toe
collocations.zh: 被从头到脚地照顾周到

derivatives.zh: 被娇惯的；养尊处优的（动词加 -ed 构成形容词）
溺爱；悉心照料（动词加 -ing 构成动名词）
娇惯别人的人（动词加 -er 表施动者）

senses.title: To treat someone with too much kindness
senses.definition: to treat a person or animal with excessive kindness and attention, often so that they become less able to cope
senses.definitionCN: 对人或者动物过度体贴宠爱，常常使他们变得难以吃苦
senses.example: Her grandmother pampered the child with sweets and toys.
senses.exampleCN: 外婆用糖果和玩具娇惯这个孩子。
senses.why: The old English sense is to feed someone richly, so the core image of over-caring begins with food and comfort.
senses.whyCN: pamper 的古英语义就是把人喂得饱饱的，所以「过度照料」的核心意象从吃与舒适开始。

senses.title: To look after someone extremely well
senses.definition: to take such good care of someone that they feel comfortable and relaxed
senses.definitionCN: 把某人照顾得极好，使其感到舒适放松
senses.example: The hotel pampered every guest with warm towels and tea.
senses.exampleCN: 酒店为每位客人递上热毛巾和热茶，把他们照顾得无微不至。
senses.why: Once the over-caring sense loses its criticism, the same word simply means treating someone very well.
senses.whyCN: 当「过分照料」的贬义褪去，同一个词就单纯表示把人照顾得非常好。

senses.title: To give oneself a treat
senses.definition: to allow yourself an expensive or enjoyable experience as a reward
senses.definitionCN: 允许自己享受昂贵或者令人愉快的体验，作为奖赏
senses.example: After the exams she pampered herself with a day at the spa.
senses.exampleCN: 考试结束后，她到水疗中心待了一天犒劳自己。
senses.why: In modern use the object can be oneself, so pampering becomes a self-directed reward.
senses.whyCN: 现代用法中宾语可以是自己，于是 pamper 变成一种自我奖赏。

senses.title: To indulge a desire or habit
senses.definition: to allow a desire or bad habit to be satisfied rather than controlled
senses.definitionCN: 让某种欲望或者坏习惯得到满足，而不加约束
senses.example: He pampered his sweet tooth with cake every afternoon.
senses.exampleCN: 他每天下午都用蛋糕纵容自己的甜食瘾。
senses.why: When the thing being fed is a desire rather than a person, the word shifts to indulgence.
senses.whyCN: 当被喂饱的是欲望而不是人时，这个词就转指放纵。

senses.title: To comfort a body part
senses.definition: to treat an aching or tired part of the body with gentle care
senses.definitionCN: 对身体某处酸痛或者疲劳的部位温柔护理
senses.example: She pampered her tired feet with a warm soak.
senses.exampleCN: 她用温水泡脚，细心照料疲惫的双脚。
senses.why: The food-and-care image extends to the body itself, which can be fed with rest and warmth.
senses.whyCN: 「喂养与照料」的意象延伸到身体本身，可以用休息和温暖来滋补它。

senses.title: To flatter in order to please
senses.definition: to treat someone with flattering attention, sometimes to win favour
senses.definitionCN: 用恭维和体贴讨好某人，有时是为了换取好处
senses.example: The new intern pampered the director with compliments.
senses.exampleCN: 新来的实习生用恭维话讨好主任。
senses.why: Kindness can be used as a tool, so pampering gains a social sense of flattery or courtship of favour.
senses.whyCN: 善意也可以被当作工具，于是 pamper 带上了讨好、笼络的社会含义。

senses.title: Pampered as an adjective
senses.titleCN: 娇生惯养的（形容词用法）
senses.definition: describing someone who has always had everything done for them
senses.definitionCN: 形容一个人凡事都有人替他做好、从没受过苦
senses.example: He is far too pampered to live on his own.
senses.exampleCN: 他太娇生惯养了，根本没法独自生活。
senses.why: The past participle freezes the result of years of over-caring into a personal trait.
senses.whyCN: 过去分词把长年过度照料的结果固定为一个人的性格特征。

senses.title: Pampering as a noun
senses.definition: the experience of being carefully and richly treated
senses.definitionCN: 被人周到奢华地款待的体验
senses.example: A weekend of pampering at the resort did her good.
senses.exampleCN: 在度假村享受了一个周末的呵护，她感觉好多了。
senses.why: The gerund turns the repeated act of over-caring into an experience that can be bought and enjoyed.
senses.whyCN: 动名词把反复发生的过度照料变成一种可以购买、可以享受的体验。

intro.en: Pamper is first recorded in English in the fourteenth century, probably from Middle Dutch and related to German dialects meaning to cram with food.
intro.cn: pamper 在十四世纪首次见于英语，一般认为来自中古荷兰语，与德语方言中「把食物塞满」的说法同源。

items.en: A Low German verb of the form pamperen means to stuff with food; the exact written form is not certain.
items.cn: 低地德语中的一个动词，一般认为作 pamperen，意为「塞饱、喂饱」；确切写法尚不确定。

items.en: The word first appears in English with the sense of cramming someone with food.
items.cn: 该词最早以「把人塞饱」的意思出现在英语中。

items.en: The sense widens from feeding to over-feeding with comfort and kindness.
items.cn: 含义从喂饱扩大到用舒适与好意在情感上「喂撑」一个人。

items.en: Pampered is used of a spoiled favourite or a child raised too softly.
items.cn: pampered 开始用于形容被宠坏的心腹或者养得太娇气的孩子。

items.en: The link with food fades, and pamper comes to mean treating well in general.
items.cn: 与食物的联系淡去，pamper 泛化为一般意义上的「款待、呵护」。

items.en: Today pamper yourself is a common phrase in advertising and travel writing.
items.cn: 今天 pamper yourself 已成为广告和旅游文案中的常用说法。

note.en: Pamper sits between cosset and spoil, and is close to cockle, coddle, and mollycoddle in British dialect.
note.cn: pamper 处在 cosset 与 spoil 之间，并与英式方言里的 cockle、coddle、mollycoddle 意义相邻。

entries.definition: a very short printed booklet
entries.definitionCN: 小册子；只是拼写开头相近，词源不同

entries.definition: the wide grassy plains of South America
entries.definitionCN: 南美大草原；只是拼写相近，词源来自南美土语，与 pamper 无关

entries.definition: treated with too much kindness
entries.definitionCN: 被娇惯的；由 pamper 加 -ed 构成

entries.definition: to protect and treat someone too kindly
entries.definitionCN: 溺爱；格外呵护

entries.definition: to harm someone by giving them everything they want
entries.definitionCN: 宠坏；惯坏（比 pamper 更强调后果）

entries.definition: to allow yourself or another to have what is wanted
entries.definitionCN: 放纵；纵容

normalIntro.en: Pamper keeps its old food image: to pamper is to keep feeding someone comfort until they are full.
normalIntro.cn: pamper 保留了古老的「食物」意象：娇惯就是把舒适一口口喂给别人，直到他「饱了」。

normal.en: The Middle Dutch source meant to stuff with food, and that eating image survives in pamper.
normal.cn: 中古荷兰语词源意为「塞满食物」，这个吃东西的画面残留在 pamper 里。

normal.en: Pampered and pampering both come straight from the verb, one as a trait and one as an experience.
normal.cn: pampered 与 pampering 都直接来自这个动词，一个是一贯的特征，一个是一次的体验。

normal.en: Pamper a child is over-care, while pamper yourself is a reward, same verb, different tone.
normal.cn: pamper a child 是过分照料，pamper yourself 是奖赏自己，同一个动词，语气不同。

normal.en: Compare spoil: spoiling damages someone, pampering may only soften them.
normal.cn: 对比 spoil：宠坏会真的伤害一个人，而 pamper 更多只是让人变得娇气。

normal.en: Cosset, coddle, and mollycoddle are dialect cousins with the same soft caring image.
normal.cn: cosset、coddle、mollycoddle 都是方言中的近亲，共享同样柔软的照料意象。

abstract.en: Picture a spoon held out again and again to a child who is already full.
abstract.cn: 想象一把勺子一次又一次伸向已经吃饱的孩子。

abstract.en: Imagine a hotel bed with five plumped pillows and a tray of warm tea.
abstract.cn: 想象一张铺着五个蓬松枕头、旁边放着热茶的酒店大床。

abstract.en: Think of a cat curled in the sun while the owner brings the bowl to its chin.
abstract.cn: 想象一只猫躺在阳光里打盹，主人把饭盆端到它下巴底下。

examples.en: My aunt has always pampered her dog with the best food.
examples.cn: 我阿姨一直用最好的食物娇养她的狗。

examples.en: Take a day off and pamper yourself for once.
examples.cn: 休息一天，这一次好好犒劳自己吧。

examples.en: The spa offers a pampering afternoon for new mothers.
examples.cn: 这家水疗中心为新手妈妈提供一个享受呵护的下午。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「怕没盆」——怕孩子吃饭没盆子，赶紧把好吃的端过去，娇惯坏了；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 中古荷兰语 pamperen（塞饱、喂饱，存疑）→ 十四世纪英语 pamper（把人喂饱）→ 十六世纪后由「喂饱」转为「用善待把人惯坏」→ 现代英语「娇惯；呵护」。核心义为「过度喂养与照料」。

sensesIntro.en: Pamper starts from over-feeding a person, moves to treating them too kindly, then to the neutral sense of looking after someone wonderfully, and finally branches into self-reward and indulgence.
sensesIntro.cn: pamper 从把人喂得过饱出发，转为对某人过分宠爱，再褪去贬义成为「精心照料」，最后分出犒劳自己与放纵欲望两支。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a spoon held to the mouth of someone who no longer needs it.
core.cn: 核心意象：勺子一直递到已经不需要的人嘴边。

branches.en: Overfeeding becomes over-caring and spoiling.
branches.cn: 「喂饱」演变为过分照料与娇惯。

branches.en: The same picture without criticism is warm care or luxury.
branches.cn: 同一画面去掉批评色彩，就是温暖照料或者奢华享受。

branches.en: Feeding turns inward: you pamper yourself or your desires.
branches.cn: 喂养的方向转向内部：犒劳自己或者纵容欲望。

branches.en: The body itself can be the thing that is fed and comforted.
branches.cn: 身体本身也可以是被喂饱、被安慰的对象。

branches.en: Flattery, personality, and experience are the social and grammatical extensions.
branches.cn: 讨好、个人特征与体验，是这个词在社会与语法层面的延伸。

intro.en: Pamper is an English verb of Dutch origin, with no living prefix or suffix, but its -ed and -ing forms are built like any English verb.
intro.cn: pamper 源自荷兰语的英语动词，本身不含活的词缀，但它的 -ed 与 -ing 形式和普通英语动词一样构成。

latinIntro.en: Pamper is a Germanic loanword, so it has no Latin ancestor; the nearest Latin relatives belong to the near synonyms spoil and indulge.
latinIntro.cn: pamper 是日耳曼语借词，没有拉丁语祖先；最接近的拉丁同源词属于近义词 spoil 与 indulge。

items.example: The Dutch source gives the eating image.
items.exampleCN: 荷兰语词源提供了「吃」的意象。

items.example: Pamper keeps the transitive force.
items.exampleCN: pamper 保留了及物动词的力度。

items.example: The suffix -er forms pamperer.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -er 构成 pamperer。

items.example: A pamperer never says no.

definition_zh: 小册子；传单；时政短论
definition_en: a thin book with a paper cover and only a few pages, often giving information or an opinion
core_image: 一只手从一叠小书里抽出一本薄薄的小册子
scene: 车站出口，穿马甲的志愿者把一本薄薄的手册塞进路人手里。A volunteer handed out a thin pamphlet about safe cycling.
sceneCN: 这里 pamphlet 是「小册子」（第 1 个义项：几页纸的薄册子）；句意：一名志愿者分发了一本关于安全骑行的小册子。

pos.zh: 小册子；薄册
传单；宣传品
时政短论；小册子式的文章

写小册子；发表小册子攻击（名词动用）
用小册子宣传；写成小册子（pamphlet 加 -ize）

senses.title: A short paper-covered booklet
senses.definition: a small book of a few pages with a paper cover, giving facts or guidance
senses.definitionCN: 只有几页、纸质封面的小书，用来说明事实或者提供指导
senses.example: The museum gives out a free pamphlet at the door.
senses.exampleCN: 博物馆在门口免费发放一本小册子。
senses.why: The name comes from a popular love poem, so the small unbound booklet is the oldest and central sense.
senses.whyCN: 这个词的名字来自一首流行的情诗，所以最早、最核心的义项就是这种薄薄的散页小书。

senses.title: A leaflet for advertising or a cause
senses.definition: a printed sheet or thin booklet used to promote a product, a service, or a campaign
senses.definitionCN: 用来宣传产品、服务或者某项运动的印刷纸张或者薄册
senses.example: Protesters were handing out pamphlets in the square.
senses.exampleCN: 抗议者正在广场上分发传单。
senses.why: Once cheap printing made small sheets easy to give away, the pamphlet became a tool for reaching crowds.
senses.whyCN: 廉价印刷使小纸册可以随手赠送之后，pamphlet 就成了向人群传播信息的工具。

senses.title: A short essay that attacks or argues
senses.definition: a short essay printed on its own that argues a political or religious position
senses.definitionCN: 单独印行的短文，论证某个政治或者宗教立场
senses.example: His pamphlet on the new tax was read across the colonies.
senses.exampleCN: 他那篇关于新税的小册子在各个殖民地都被人传阅。
senses.why: Before newspapers were common, a cheap short essay was the fastest way to argue in public.
senses.whyCN: 在报纸普及之前，一篇便宜的短文是公开辩论最快的武器。

senses.title: In modern publishing, a thin bound file
senses.titleCN: 薄册；文件册（现代出版用法）
senses.definition: a publication of fewer than a set number of pages, usually without a hard cover
senses.definitionCN: 页数少于规定数目、通常没有硬封面的出版物
senses.example: The library files each pamphlet in a separate box.
senses.exampleCN: 图书馆把每本薄册分别装进一个盒子。
senses.why: Libraries and publishers needed a tidy label for short printed works, so pamphlet became a format term.
senses.whyCN: 图书馆和出版社需要给短篇印刷品一个整齐的名称，于是 pamphlet 变成了格式术语。

senses.title: A brief guide for using something
senses.definition: a short printed guide that explains how to use a product or service
senses.definitionCN: 简短印刷的指南，说明怎样使用某个产品或服务
senses.example: Read the pamphlet before you switch on the machine.
senses.exampleCN: 开机之前先读一读说明书。
senses.why: Instruction can be short enough for a few pages, so the format name takes on the role of a manual.
senses.whyCN: 说明也可以短到只需几页，于是这个格式名就承担了说明书的功能。

senses.title: The general idea of brief printed matter
senses.definition: printed leaflets and booklets considered together as a kind of material
senses.definitionCN: 把传单和小册子合在一起，作为一种印刷材料来看
senses.example: Shelves of pamphlets crowd the local history room.
senses.exampleCN: 当地历史资料室里堆满了成排的宣传册。
senses.why: When many short items are collected, the singular word can label the whole class of them.
senses.whyCN: 当许多小册子被收集在一起时，这个词就用来称呼这一整类东西。

senses.title: A fleeting, thin thing
senses.titleCN: 薄薄的一叠；短暂的东西
senses.definition: in older or playful use, a very thin or slight object
senses.definitionCN: 在较旧或者戏谑的用法中，指非常单薄的东西
senses.example: He wore his hair as thin as a pamphlet.
senses.exampleCN: 他的头发稀疏得像一本小册子。
senses.why: The chief feeling of a pamphlet is thinness, and thinness invites comic comparison.
senses.whyCN: pamphlet 给人的主要感觉就是薄，而薄很容易被拿来做喜剧化的比喻。

intro.en: Pamphlet comes from Pamphilus, the title of a twelfth-century Latin love poem, whose short unbound copies English listeners nicknamed pamphilets.
intro.cn: pamphlet 来自十二世纪拉丁文情诗《Pamphilus》的题名，这本诗被印成薄薄的散页小册，英语听众把它戏称为 pamphilet。

items.en: Pamphilus is the name of a poem on love, probably borrowed from the Greek name of a famous love poem.
items.cn: Pamphilus 是一首情诗的名字，一般认为借自一首著名希腊情诗的人名。

items.en: The short popular poem was printed in thin unbound sheets, and the sheetlets were called pamphilets.
items.cn: 这首流行短诗以薄薄的散页印行，这些小册页被称为 pamphilet。

items.en: The ending shifts to -let, the common English suffix for something small.
items.cn: 词尾被重新理解成 -let，即英语中常见的表示「小」的后缀。

items.en: Any small unbound printed book, especially a short essay on a public question, is called a pamphlet.
items.cn: 任何薄薄的散页印刷小书，尤其是论述公共问题的短文，都被称为 pamphlet。

items.en: Pamphlet wars rage in England, and pamphleteer names the writers who fight in them.
items.cn: 英国爆发小册子论战，pamphleteer 用来称呼这些论战的作者。

items.en: Today a pamphlet is usually an advertising or information leaflet, and sometimes a thin official booklet.
items.cn: 今天 pamphlet 多半指广告或者说明传单，有时也指薄薄的官方小册。

note.en: Pamphlet is a false relative of Pamphilus, and it shares the printed-matter field with brochure, leaflet, booklet, and flyer.
note.cn: pamphlet 与 Pamphilus 是假同源关系，它与 brochure、leaflet、booklet、flyer 同属一个印刷品义场。

entries.definitionCN: 娇惯；只是拼写开头相近，词源不同

entries.definition: a writer of short political pamphlets
entries.definitionCN: 小册子作者；由 pamphlet 加 -eer 构成

entries.definition: soft brushed cloth
entries.definitionCN: 法兰绒；只是拼写相近，词源来自威尔士语，与 pamphlet 无关

entries.definition: a thin book with pictures that advertises something
entries.definitionCN: 宣传画册；比 pamphlet 更强调图片与推销

entries.definition: a single printed sheet, often folded
entries.definitionCN: 传单；单张纸，通常折叠

entries.definitionCN: 小册子；中性说法，不带政治色彩

normalIntro.en: Pamphlet hides the name of an old love poem, and it ends with the little suffix -let.
normalIntro.cn: pamphlet 里藏着一首古老情诗的名字，结尾的 -let 则是表示「小」的后缀。

normal.en: The -let ending is the same little word-maker as in booklet and leaflet.
normal.cn: 结尾的 -let 与 booklet、leaflet 里的是同一个表「小」的构词成分。

normal.en: Pamphlet began as a nickname for thin copies of a poem, so thinness is built into it.
normal.cn: pamphlet 最初是那首诗的薄本的外号，所以「薄」是它自带的含义。

normal.en: Add -eer and you get pamphleteer, a person who writes these short arguments.
normal.cn: 加上 -eer 就得到 pamphleteer，指专门写这类短论的人。

normal.en: Hand out pamphlets is the fixed partnership you hear at any campaign.
normal.cn: 在任何一场宣传活动中你听到的都是 hand out pamphlets 这个固定搭配。

normal.en: Compare brochure, which means to stitch together and stresses glossy pictures, not thinness.
normal.cn: 对比 brochure：它原意是「缝线装订」，强调光亮的图片而不是薄。

abstract.en: Picture a hand pulling one thin sheet from a fan of them.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手从扇形摊开的一摞纸里抽出一张薄纸。

abstract.en: Imagine a volunteer in a vest pushing paper into a stranger palm.
abstract.cn: 想象一个穿马甲的志愿者把纸塞进陌生人的掌心。

abstract.en: Think of an old poem folded small enough to fit a pocket.
abstract.cn: 想象一首旧诗被折得很小，正好塞进口袋。

examples.en: The clinic has a pamphlet explaining how to store medicine safely.
examples.cn: 诊所有一本讲如何安全存放药品的小册子。

examples.en: Political pamphlets were passed around in secret.
examples.cn: 政治小册子在暗中流传。

examples.en: She wrote a pamphlet against the new factory.
examples.cn: 她写了一篇反对新工厂的小册子。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「盘佛来」——盘子里摊开一叠薄纸，佛来了也递上一张；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 中世纪拉丁语 Pamphilus（情诗题名，一般认为源自希腊人名）→ 中古英语 pamphilet（该诗的散页薄本）→ 词尾被同化为表「小」的 -let → 十六世纪泛指薄册子与时政短文。核心义为「薄薄的散页印刷品」。

sensesIntro.en: From a thinly printed poem, pamphlet widens to any small unbound booklet, then to campaign leaflets, then to short printed arguments, and finally to a general label for brief print.
sensesIntro.cn: pamphlet 从薄薄印行的一首诗，扩大到任何小散页册子，再扩展到宣传传单、印刷短论，最后成为短篇印刷品的通称。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a few folded sheets pressed into a hand.
core.cn: 核心意象：几页折叠的纸被塞进一只手里。

branches.en: The thin paper booklet is the direct heir of the old pamphlet nickname.
branches.cn: 薄纸小册子是古老戏称最直接的继承者。

branches.en: Cheap printing turns the booklet into a giveaway leaflet.
branches.cn: 廉价印刷让薄册子变成随手赠送的传单。

branches.en: The format becomes a channel for argument and a library category.
branches.cn: 这种形式既是论辩的渠道，也成为图书馆的分类。

branches.en: Short guides and gathered propaganda inherit the same shape.
branches.cn: 简短指南与汇编的宣传品继承同样的外形。

branches.en: Thinness itself can be borrowed as a figure of speech.
branches.cn: 「薄」本身也可以被借来做修辞比喻。

intro.en: Pamphlet looks like it has a suffix, but the -let was refashioned from the end of a poem title, and later writers added -eer and -ize.
intro.cn: pamphlet 看起来带后缀，但 -let 是从诗名末尾改来的，后来作者又加上 -eer 与 -ize。

latinIntro.en: The base is medieval Latin Pamphilus, a proper name, so the Latin relatives here are a name rather than a root meaning thin.
latinIntro.cn: 词基是中世纪拉丁语专名 Pamphilus，所以这里的拉丁同源成分是一个人名，而不是表示「薄」的词根。

items.example: Pamphilus gave the word its first syllable set.
items.exampleCN: Pamphilus 提供了这个词开头的音节。

items.example: Pamphilet first names the tiny copies.
items.exampleCN: pamphilet 最初指那些小薄本。

items.example: The suffix -let forms booklet and leaflet.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -let 构成 booklet 与 leaflet。

items.example: Pamphlet settles into its modern spelling.
items.exampleCN: pamphlet 固定为现代拼写。

items.example: The suffix -eer forms pamphleteer.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -eer 构成 pamphleteer。

items.example: Pamphleteer names a political writer.
items.exampleCN: pamphleteer 指政治性的小册子作者。

items.example: The suffix -ize forms pamphletize.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ize 构成 pamphletize。

items.example: Pamphletize means to go about in print.
items.exampleCN: pamphletize 表示用小册子四处宣传。

items.meaning: of the nature of a pamphlet
items.example: Pamphletary prose is short and sharp.
items.exampleCN: 小册子式的文章短小犀利。

latinEntries.meaningCN: 一部爱情喜剧诗的题名

latinEntries.meaningCN: 书；树的内皮（拉丁语中「书」的原义，与 booklet 义场相关）

definition_zh: 全景；全景图；全貌；综合概览
definition_en: a view of a wide area seen from one point, or a complete picture of events over a period
core_image: 站在山顶转一圈，四周的景色连成一整幅画
scene: 清早，游客沿着石阶爬上山头，转着身子向四面看，山谷河流尽收眼底。From the top of the hill, the whole town spread out in a wide panorama.
sceneCN: 这里 panorama 是「全景」（第 1 个义项：从一处看到的辽阔景象）；句意：从山顶望去，整座小镇铺展成一幅宽阔的全景。

pos.zh: 全景；全景图；全貌
综合概览

collocations.zh: 全景画廊（十九世纪专展全景画的圆形展厅）

以全景的方式（panoramic 加 -ally 构成副词）
全景画画家（panorama 加 -ist 表艺人）

senses.title: A wide view from one point
senses.definition: a view in which a large area of land or city can be seen from a single place
senses.definitionCN: 从一个地方能看到大片地区或者整座城市的视野
senses.example: We climbed the tower for a panorama of the harbour.
senses.exampleCN: 我们爬上塔楼，欣赏港口全景。
senses.why: The Greek parts mean all and sight, so the first meaning is a single view that takes in everything around.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语的两个部分分别表示「全部」与「景象」，所以第一个义项就是一眼看遍四周的视野。

senses.title: A continuous painted picture of a scene
senses.definition: a large picture displayed on the inside of a curved wall so that viewers feel surrounded
senses.definitionCN: 画在弧形墙内侧的大幅画，让观者觉得自己被景色包围
senses.example: The museum still has a painted panorama of the old siege.
senses.exampleCN: 博物馆里还保存着一幅描绘旧日围城战的全景画。
senses.why: Painting the whole sweep of a view onto a curved wall was the technical ancestor of the word.
senses.whyCN: 把一整片视野画到弧形墙上，正是这个词在技术上的祖先。

senses.title: A complete survey of a subject
senses.definition: a complete account of a field or period, covering it from every side
senses.definitionCN: 对某个领域或者时期从头到尾、面面俱到的叙述
senses.example: The book offers a panorama of modern art.
senses.exampleCN: 这本书呈现出现代艺术的全貌。
senses.why: Seeing everything at once becomes seeing a whole topic at once, so a survey is a panorama in time.
senses.whyCN: 一次看遍全部景象，就变成一次看遍整个话题，于是在时间维度上也出现了全景。

senses.title: The constantly changing scene
senses.definition: a scene or situation that keeps changing, described in the way a landscape is
senses.definitionCN: 不断变化的情景或者局面，用描写风景方式去描写它
senses.example: The panorama of village life kept shifting with each season.
senses.exampleCN: 乡村生活的图景随着季节不断变换。
senses.why: A wide view always includes change, so the word can name the changing scene itself rather than a still picture.
senses.whyCN: 辽阔的视野本来就包含变化，所以这个词也能指变化中的景象，而不只是一幅静止的画。

senses.title: An unfolding sequence of events
senses.definition: the way a story or sequence of events passes before the mind like a long view
senses.definitionCN: 故事或者一连串事件在脑海中像长卷一样铺开的样子
senses.example: The year passed like a panorama before her.
senses.exampleCN: 这一年像一幅长卷从她眼前掠过。
senses.why: If a landscape has sides, a lifetime has stages, so the word stretches to events that pass in order.
senses.whyCN: 风景有左右两面，人生也有各个阶段，于是这个词又延伸到按顺序展开的事件。

senses.title: A photographic or digital wide image
senses.definition: a photograph or digital image made by joining several shots into one very wide view
senses.definitionCN: 把多张照片拼接成一整幅极宽的图像或者照片
senses.example: My phone builds a panorama from four shots.
senses.exampleCN: 我的手机用四张照片合成一张全景图。
senses.why: Cameras that swing round can record the whole view, so the painted panorama returns as a digital object.
senses.whyCN: 能旋转取景的相机可以记录整个视野，于是画出来的全景又变成了数字图像。

senses.title: A panned head movement
senses.definition: the act of turning the eyes or head slowly across a whole scene
senses.definitionCN: 眼睛或者头部缓慢地扫过整个场景的动作
senses.example: He took in the room in one slow panorama.
senses.exampleCN: 他慢慢环视一周，把整个房间看了个遍。
senses.why: The physical turning needed to see everything is the live version of the painted panorama.
senses.whyCN: 为了看全面所需的转身动作，就是全景画在真实世界中的即时版本。

intro.en: Panorama was invented in 1792 by the painter Robert Barker for a large curved picture, joining Greek pan, meaning all, and horama, meaning a view.
intro.cn: panorama 由画家罗伯特·巴克于 1792 年造出，用于命名一幅巨大的弧形画作，由希腊语 pan（全部）与 horama（景象）合成。

items.en: Pan means all or whole, and horama means that which is seen.
items.cn: pan 意为全部、整个，horama 意为所见之物。

items.en: Robert Barker patents a curved painted view and names it panorama.
items.cn: 罗伯特·巴克为弧形绘景申请专利，把它命名为 panorama。

items.en: Panorama rooms spread across Europe and America, and pamphlet guides to the views appear.
items.cn: 全景展厅在欧洲和美洲流行起来，还出现了介绍这些全景画的小册子。

items.en: The word leaves the exhibition hall for mountains, cities, and any wide view.
items.cn: 这个词走出展厅，用于形容山景、城市以及任何辽阔的视野。

items.en: The adjective panoramic is coined, and the metaphor extends to history and events.
items.cn: 形容词 panoramic 出现，这个比喻也延伸到历史与事件。

items.en: Cameras and phones offer panorama modes, reviving the word as a format name.
items.cn: 相机和手机提供全景模式，让这个词再次成为格式名称。

note.en: Panorama shares its pan- first syllable with pantomime and pandemic, and its sense of wide seeing with vista, view, and prospect.
note.cn: panorama 与 pantomime、pandemic 共享开头的 pan-，又与 vista、view、prospect 同属「开阔视野」的义场。

entries.definition: showing or taking in a wide view
entries.definitionCN: 全景的；由 panorama 加 -ic 构成

entries.definition: a show acted without words
entries.definitionCN: 哑剧；同样以希腊语 pan 开头，但后半部是「模仿」，与 panorama 不同源

entries.definition: a disease spreading through a whole population
entries.definitionCN: 瘟疫；同样以 pan 开头，但表示「全部人群」，与 panorama 不同源

entries.definition: a long narrow view, especially through an opening
entries.definitionCN: 长条形远景；常指向远处的一条视野

entries.definition: what can be seen from a place
entries.definitionCN: 视野；景色（最普通的说法）

entries.definition: a wide view, or what may happen in the future
entries.definitionCN: 远景；也指前景，比 panorama 更偏未来

normalIntro.en: Panorama is built from pan, meaning all, and horama, meaning sight, so it is literally an all-sight.
normalIntro.cn: panorama 由 pan（全部）与 horama（景象）构成，字面意思就是「全都看得见的景象」。

normal.en: The prefix pan- in panorama is the same all in pandemic and pantheism.
normal.cn: panorama 里的前缀 pan- 与 pandemic、pantheism 中的是同一个「全」。

normal.en: The adjective is panoramic, dropping the final -a and adding -ic.
normal.cn: 形容词是 panoramic，去掉词尾的 -a 再加 -ic。

normal.en: Panorama began as a trade name for a painted room, so it still feels like a format as well as a view.
normal.cn: panorama 最初是一间绘画展厅的商品名，所以它今天既指视野也像一种格式。

normal.en: Compare vista: a vista is a narrow far view, a panorama takes in the wide sweep.
normal.cn: 对比 vista：vista 是狭长的远景，panorama 是一大片的广阔视野。

normal.en: A panorama of history is a complete survey, while a view of history is only one opinion.
normal.cn: a panorama of history 是完整的概览，而 a view of history 只是某一种看法。

abstract.en: Picture yourself turning slowly on a hilltop with the horizon closing into a ring.
abstract.cn: 想象自己在山顶缓缓转身，地平线连成一个圆环。

abstract.en: Imagine standing in a round hall that is painted all the way up to the sky.
abstract.cn: 想象站在一个一直画到天空的圆形大厅里。

abstract.en: Think of a phone sweeping sideways to stitch four shots into one long picture.
abstract.cn: 想象手机横向扫过，把四张照片拼接成一幅长图。

examples.en: The summit offers a panorama of snow peaks on every side.
examples.cn: 山顶四面都是雪峰构成的辽阔全景。

examples.en: The exhibition gives a panorama of life in the city a century ago.
examples.cn: 这次展览呈现了一个世纪前这座城市生活的全貌。

examples.en: This camera can capture a full panorama in one press.
examples.cn: 这台相机一按快门就能拍下完整全景。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「怕拿马」——怕拿不住马，干脆站在山头转一圈，把马群的全景看遍；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 希腊语 pan（全部）+ horama（景象）→ 1792 年英国画家巴克造出 panorama（环视全景画）→ 十九世纪中期泛指山景城市等辽阔视野 → 后期比喻历史与事件的全貌。核心义为「一眼看遍全部景象」。

sensesIntro.en: Panorama begins as a painted curved view, leaves the gallery for real landscapes, then widens into a survey of a subject, a changing scene, a sequence of events, and finally a camera format.
sensesIntro.cn: panorama 从一幅弧形的绘画全景出发，走出画廊用于真实风景，再扩大为课题概览、变化中的景象、事件的展开，最后成为一种相机格式。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the horizon bending into a complete ring of sight.
core.cn: 核心意象：地平线弯成一整圈，所有景象首尾相接。

branches.en: The literal wide view is the primary sense.
branches.cn: 字面意义上的辽阔视野是首要义项。

branches.en: The painted version that gave the word its birth.
branches.cn: 赋予这个词生命的绘画版本。

branches.en: Topic surveys and changing scenes are the spatial image in abstract form.
branches.cn: 课题概览与变化中的景象是空间意象的抽象化。

branches.en: Events in time turn into a view stretched sideways.
branches.cn: 时间中的事件被拉成横向展开的视野。

branches.en: Captured and panned views are the technical descendants.
branches.cn: 拍摄下来的全景与转身扫视，是这个词在技术上的后代。

intro.en: Panorama is a modern coinage from two Greek combining forms, with pan- as a living English prefix and -orama too rare to build new words.
intro.cn: panorama 由两个希腊语构词成分组成的现代新造词，pan- 是活的英语前缀，-orama 则太罕见，没能造出更多新词。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin ancestor here; the parts are Greek, and the Greek compounds sight and all are the nearest relatives.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有拉丁语祖先，构词成分都是希腊语，最接近的同族就是希腊语中表示「景象」与「全部」的复合形式。

items.example: The prefix pan- forms pandemic and pan-Asian.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 pan- 构成 pandemic 与 pan-Asian。

items.meaning: a sight, that which is seen
items.example: Horama supplies the seeing half.
items.exampleCN: horama 提供了「看见」的那一半。

items.example: The ending -oma forms the noun horama.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -oma 构成名词 horama。

items.example: Panorama was patented as a trade name.
items.exampleCN: panorama 曾作为商品名被申请专利。

items.example: The suffix -ic forms panoramic.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ic 构成 panoramic。

items.example: A panoramic window is common in cars.
items.exampleCN: 汽车上常见全景天窗。

items.example: The suffix -ally forms panoramically.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ally 构成 panoramically。

items.example: The suffix -ist forms panoramist.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ist 构成 panoramist。

items.example: A panoramist needed a very long canvas.
items.exampleCN: 全景画画家需要一块很长的画布。

scene: 旅人终于爬上山顶，回身一转，整座山谷骤然展开在眼前。From the summit we enjoyed a panoramic view of the valley.
sceneCN: 这里 panoramic 是「全景的」（第 1 个义项：视野完整而宽广）；句意：站在山顶，我们欣赏到了山谷的全景。

以全景方式；概括地

senses.title: Giving a wide, complete view
senses.definition: showing a wide, complete view of a place or landscape from one point
senses.definitionCN: 从一点所能看到的宽广而完整的地方或风景
senses.example: The hotel room has a panoramic view of the bay.
senses.exampleCN: 酒店房间可以看到海湾的全景。
senses.why: The Greek base horan means to see, so the adjective names a view that takes in the whole scene at once.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语词根基 horan 意为「看见」，因此这个形容词描述的是把整个场面一眼尽收的视野。

senses.title: Broad in scope
senses.definition: covering a subject widely and in outline rather than in detail
senses.definitionCN: 对某一主题作广泛而概要的涵盖，而非细究细节
senses.example: The opening chapter gives a panoramic survey of modern history.
senses.exampleCN: 开篇一章对现代史做了全景式的概述。
senses.why: From a wide look at a landscape the word moves to a wide look at ideas, keeping the same whole-scene shape.
senses.whyCN: 从对景色的宽视野迁移到对思想的宽视野，保留了「整体尽收」的同一构形。

senses.title: Sweeping and continuous
senses.titleCN: 绵延不断的；横贯视野的
senses.definition: extending continuously across a wide field of vision, as a road or a chain of hills
senses.definitionCN: 像道路或山峦那样横贯开阔视野、绵延不断
senses.example: A panoramic belt of forest runs along the river.
senses.exampleCN: 一条绵延不断的森林带沿着河流延伸。
senses.why: A panorama is also a picture unrolled as one long sheet, so the adjective can describe things that spread across the eye like a painted scroll.
senses.whyCN: panorama 一词也指展开的长卷画，因此这个词可以形容像画卷一样在眼前铺开的事物。

senses.title: Suitable for a full scene
senses.definition: designed to record or display a very wide area, as in cameras or screens
senses.definitionCN: 用于拍摄或显示极宽阔范围的，如相机、屏幕
senses.example: This phone has a panoramic mode for wide landscapes.
senses.exampleCN: 这部手机有拍摄宽幅风景的全景模式。
senses.why: Once the eye could travel the whole scene, machines were built to capture it, and the adjective came to label the tool.
senses.whyCN: 眼睛能纵览全场景之后，人们又造出捕捉全场景的机器，这个词便转而标注工具本身。

senses.title: Figurative overall impression
senses.definition: giving a broad overall impression rather than a narrow or close one
senses.definitionCN: 给出宽阔而总括的印象，而非狭窄或贴近的看法
senses.example: Take a panoramic look at the whole project before you start.
senses.exampleCN: 开工前先对整个项目作一次鸟瞰式的了解。
senses.why: The physical high vantage point becomes a mental vantage point, letting the adjective describe understanding rather than eyesight.
senses.whyCN: 现实中的高处视点转化为思维上的高点，使这个形容词可以描述理解力而不是视力。

intro.en: Panoramic is the adjective of panorama, a word coined in the late eighteenth century from Greek pan, all, plus horama, a view.
intro.cn: panoramic 是 panorama 的形容词形式；panorama 是十八世纪末由希腊语 pan「全部」加 horama「所见之物」新造的词。

items.en: Pan means all or every, and horan is the verb to see; horama is the thing seen, a sight.
items.cn: pan 意为全部、每一个；horan 是动词「看见」；horama 指所见之物、景象。

items.en: The elements were never joined in ancient Greek as one word; the compound of pan and horama was put together later, by English speakers rather than by Greek speakers.
items.cn: 这些成分从未在古希腊语中合为一个词；pan 与 horama 的组合是后人、主要是英语使用者拼接的。

items.en: The noun panorama is credited to the painter Robert Barker for a circular painting shown in London in 1796; the date of the first printed use is uncertain.
items.cn: 名词 panorama 一般认为出自画家罗伯特·巴克，他于 1796 年在伦敦展出环形画；首次见于印刷物的年代不确定。

items.en: Because panorama ended in the common noun suffix -ama, later coinages copied the pattern, giving cyclorama, diorama and others.
items.cn: 由于 panorama 以常见名词后缀 -ama 结尾，后来的新造词纷纷仿效，产生 cyclorama、diorama 等。

items.en: The adjective panoramic followed the noun, first describing paint and scenery and later any broad, overall view.
items.cn: 形容词 panoramic 随后而来，先形容绘画与风景，后来泛指任何宽阔、总括的看法。

note.en: Panoramic belongs to the family of panorama and shares its Greek seeing elements; near meanings cluster around words for wide and comprehensive views.
note.cn: panoramic 与 panorama 同属一词族，共享希腊语中表示「看」的成分；近义方向则是「宽阔」与「全面」两类词。

entries.definition: wide in range and ignoring detail

entries.definition: covering a large area or scope

entries.definition: giving a wide view from above
